title: Animation markers deleted after re-import
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2-stable and 4.8-beta1

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:36:46 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (nvidia; 615.78.08) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 62.54 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Surround 7.1)

### Issue description

When importing a glb file with an animation, if "Save to File" is enabled and "Keep Custom Tracks" is on, while markers are saved to the file when you create them, if you reimport the glb file, the markers are deleted from the file.

I could see an argument that the "markers" are not "custom tracks" and so the "Keep Custom Tracks" shouldn't be expected to preserve them, but it seems as though they're similar enough to custom tracks that they should be preserved. The fact that they are saved to the file in the first place makes me think this is an oversight.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a glb file with an animation to the project.
2. In the Advanced Import Settings, ensure "Save to File" is "Enabled", "Keep Custom Tracks" is checked, and a Path is set.
3. Go to the imported AnimationPlayer in a scene (add the glb to a scene and check "Editable Children", or create a "New Inherited Scene")
4. Add a marker to the animation and save it. Optionally also add a custom track to it.
5. Close the scene.
6. Reimport the glb file
7. Open the scene and the markers will be gone. If you created a custom track in step 4, it will be preserved.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33568448/MRP.zip)

If you look at "dummy.tres" in the project before opening it, you'll see a "test_marker" defined on the animation. Once you open the project in godot and it does its initial import, the "test_marker" will be deleted.

title: Changing length of animation in a named AnimationLibrary doesn't update current_animation_length
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2, and in my current compiled 4.8 branch
- this is regression from 4.6, where this bug didn't happen.

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable (35e80b3a8) - cpe:/o:nixos:nixos:26.11 26.11 (Zokor) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 threads) - 15.33 GiB memory

### Issue description

If you add an Animation to an AnimationLibrary and set it playing and you dynamically change the animation's length the update doesn't get respected in the AnimationPlayer, so when you try to seek to time points outside of its cached value it clamps it to the wrong animation length.

(I'm using the feature of inserting keys into a running animation to interpolate the keyframe positions of a remote player over the network.)

### Steps to reproduce

The following prints the animation length set to 10, but the AnimationPlayer 

```GDScript
func _ready():
	var animation := Animation.new()
	animation.length = 1.0

	var track := animation.add_track(Animation.TYPE_POSITION_3D)
	animation.track_set_path(track, ^"Target")
	animation.track_insert_key(track, 0.0, Vector3.ZERO)

	var library := AnimationLibrary.new()
	library.add_animation(&"test", animation)
	$AnimationPlayer.add_animation_library(&"playeral", library)
	$AnimationPlayer.play(&"playeral/test")
	$AnimationPlayer.pause()

	# Extend the already assigned animation.
	animation.length = 10.0
	animation.track_insert_key(track, 5.0, Vector3(99, 0, 0))

	var seek_time = 5.0
	print("Seeking to ", seek_time)
	$AnimationPlayer.seek(seek_time, true)

	print("Resource length: ", animation.length)
	print("Player length:   ", $AnimationPlayer.current_animation_length)
	print("Seek position:   ", $AnimationPlayer.current_animation_position)
```

In 4.7 and 4.8 this prints:

```
Seeking to 5.0
Resource length: 10.0
Player length:   1.0
Seek position:   1.0
```

In 4.6 this prints:

```
Seeking to 5.0
Resource length: 10.0
Player length:   10.0
Seek position:   5.0
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[animation_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33555303/animation_bug.zip)

The suspect is the `AnimationLibrary.animation_changed` signal not using the full path of the animation.

title: macOS export with Shader Baker crashes on start: “Not enough bytes for uniform in shader container” (Metal, 4.7.2)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.0.stable and 4.7.2.stable (official builds)

### System information

macOS 26 (Tahoe), Apple M2 Pro, Metal 4.0 – Forward+, Xcode installed (metal/metallib toolchain available)

### Issue description

A macOS export with Shader Baker enabled crashes on start as soon as user://shader_cache is empty (fresh install). The log shows for ~21 shaders, including engine shaders such as VolumetricFogShaderRD and SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD:

ERROR: Not enough bytes for uniform in shader container.
   at: from_bytes (servers/rendering/rendering_shader_container.cpp:818)
ERROR: Failed to parse shader container from binary.
   at: shader_create_from_bytecode_with_samplers (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4179)
ERROR: Condition "shader.is_null()" is true. Returning: false
   at: _load_from_cache (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:679)
ERROR: Parameter "shader" is null.
ERROR: FATAL: Index p_index = 35 is out of bounds (size() = 0).
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 5

Same result with application/min_macos_version_arm64 = 11.00 and 15.00.
The export log contains no “requires Apple… but target is…” warnings, so no shader was marked invalid during baking.
Without Shader Baker the export works. But the first start compiles shaders for ~3.5 minutes (blocked/white screen), which is what the baker is meant to avoid.
Side effect: after the crash, the baked containers are copied to user://shader_cache, and even a later export without baker crashes until that folder is deleted.
Possibly related observation while reading the source (drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.cpp, also on master): when a shader is mark_invalid()-ed during baking, _to_bytes_reflection_binding_uniform_extra_data() and _to_bytes_shader_extra_data() write 0 bytes, but _from_bytes_reflection_binding_uniform_extra_data() / _from_bytes_shader_extra_data() always read sizeof(UniformData) / sizeof(StageData). That would produce exactly this error for invalid shaders. In our case no shader seems to be marked invalid, so there may be a second cause.

### Steps to reproduce

Forward+ project with a few 3D materials, volumetric fog / environment effects, MetalFX Temporal upscaling.
macOS export preset, Shader Baker enabled, export from the editor (not headless) to .dmg/.app.
Delete ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/<project>/shader_cache and the app’s Metal cache ($(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)<bundle id>).
Start the export

Detailed system info: 
- Gentoo Linux, kernel 7.1.3-gentoo-dist-bin
- Wayland, Hyprland

- Intel UHD Graphics 630, kernel driver i915
- NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 Mobile, proprietary driver 580.173.02

The Godot editor crashes during startup with an empty Compatibility project containing only project.godot. No scripts, scenes, plugins or GDExtensions are required.
The crash reproduces on native Wayland. It also reproduces under Xvfb with Mesa software OpenGL rendering.
The logs show the OpenGL renderer initializing on Intel, followed by Vulkan device discovery listing the NVIDIA GPU. Texture/render-target errors and shader compilation failures then occur, followed by a native crash reported as signal 11.

[application]

[rendering]

```

2. From that directory, run:
```bash
godot --editor --path . \
  --display-driver wayland \
  --rendering-driver opengl3 \
  --audio-driver Dummy \
  --verbose
```

3. Observe the native crash during editor startup.
This was also reproduced with fresh, isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME directories, excluding existing user editor settings as a requirement.

title: String.to_float() does not correctly round; reads DBL_MIN and subnormals as 0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.dev [4d10419ca], 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf]
   - on both Linux x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS arm64
- `core/string/ustring.cpp` is basically unchanged since v1.0, so I doubt this is a regression.

### System information

macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 - Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono.official [ed1daf0bf]

### Issue description

Ran into this rounding issue when porting a game from C# to GDScript/C++ 
 
- String.to_float() does not return the nearest double; reads values below about 1e-292 as 0.
- Since #98750 and #108836 Godot writes doubles with Grisu2, so the text comes back under a correcty rounded parser, but Godot fails read back:
    - `JSON.stringify(x, "", true, true)` documents that it writes digits "to guarantee exact decoding", yet `JSON.parse_string()` returns a different double for values in practice.
    - GDScript literals with more than about 15 significant digits can compile to a neighboring double (1.44269504088896338700 is one ULP off), and 2.2250738585072014e-308 (DBL_MIN) compiles to 0.0.

- **Related issue** #123700 mentions the rounding and "1e-320" → 0 only as a "related, lower priority" note under a different bug (leading zeros), and its fix #123839 says the rounding is out of scope. Filing separately so they don't close together.
    - Both come from the same root; a correctly rounded parser fixes both, and #123700 too.

**Partial Fix**
This stop gap solution (below) prevents ~1e-292 reading as 0; the rounding needs a correctly rounded, e.g. [fast_float](https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float).

```diff
--- a/core/string/ustring.cpp
+++ b/core/string/ustring.cpp
@@ -2555,6 +2555,12 @@ static double built_in_strtod(
 		exp = maxExponent;
 		WARN_PRINT("Exponent too high");
 	}
+	// 10^exp overflows a double past 10^308, and dividing by infinity would turn values as large as
+	// 2.2250738585072014e-308 (DBL_MIN) into 0. Divide by 10^256 first so the rest stays finite.
+	if (expSign && exp > 308) {
+		fraction /= powersOf10[8];

title: Compute shader with barrier throws error when replaying push constants onto a shader that uses none
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot v4.7, Godot v4.8 (current master)

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.mono - macOS Sequoia (15.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M3 Pro (12 threads) - 18.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

### Short Description:
If a compute list sets push constants for one shader, then binds a shader that uses none, `compute_list_add_barrier()` replays the previous shader's push constants. A dev build then reports a size error.
The check returns before those bytes are recorded, so the dispatch is not given them. A barrier that stays on the same pipeline still restores that pipeline's constants.

### Steps to reproduce: 
1. Begin a compute list
2. Bind compute pipeline A with shader that using push constants. Call `compute_list_set_push_constant` and dispatch.
3. Bind compute pipeline B with a shader that not using push constants. Do not call  `compute_list_set_push_constant `.
4. Add barrier for pipeline B while it's still bound.

Editor will show following error:
```
This compute pipeline requires (0) bytes of push constant data, supplied: (4) <C++ Error> Condition "p_data_size != compute_list.validation.pipeline_push_constant_size" is true. <C++ Source> servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp @ compute_list_set_push_constant()
```

### Why this happens:
`compute_list_add_barrier()` replays push constants stored on compute list. Binding a new pipeline does not clear stored push constants size, so barrier calls compute_list_set_push_constant with old shader push constants data and size.

### Workaround:
You can explicitly call `compute_list_set_push_constant` after every pipeline bind, including shaders without push constants (just pass zero size), that way compute list will always have actual push constants state and barrier will not break.

### Steps to reproduce

You can use MRP attached to the issue
1. Run main.tscn
2. Check for errors inside editor debugger

[re-applied-push-constants-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33490775/re-applied-push-constants-mrp.zip)

title: Crash on exit when a GDExtension registers an `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` (regression from #121417)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.dev7 [c971f93e7], 4.8.dev2 [7220d456d], and a custom build of master at 12c17c187 (2026-10-01).
- Not reproducible in: 4.8.dev1 [ebbf577a0], 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf].

#121417 was merged on 2026-07-16, between dev1 (2026-07-06) and dev2 (2026-07-21).

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Unknown (27.0.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (2560x1440 @ 60.00 Hz, 2560x1440 @ 60.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M5 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M5 Pro (18 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The editor crashes on exit when a GDExtension has registered an OpenXR extension wrapper through the deprecated `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` class. An empty project with the Godot OpenXR Vendors add-on (any release up to 4.3.1) is enough; no XR setting needs to be enabled. Expected: clean exit, as in 4.7.2 and 4.8.dev1.

#121417 changed `OpenXRAPI::cleanup_extension_wrappers()` from

```cpp
		if (gdextension_extension_wrapper) {
			memdelete(gdextension_extension_wrapper);
		} else
#endif
		{
			memdelete(extension_wrapper);
		}
```

to

```cpp
		memdelete(gdextension_extension_wrapper);
#endif
		memdelete(extension_wrapper);
```

When the `dynamic_cast` succeeds, both `memdelete` calls now run on the same object, so it is freed twice and the second call crashes in `Object::_predelete()`. The null check added in #121416 does not help here, since the second pointer is dangling rather than null.

The if/else came from #88689, the fix for #88613 (same crash, same add-on). Since #104087 the deprecated class is a plain subclass of `OpenXRExtensionWrapper`, so both pointers are the same address and the `dynamic_cast` no longer serves a purpose.

Reverting the `cleanup_extension_wrappers` hunk of #121417 fixes it: with a local build of master at 12c17c187 the editor crashes on exit as above, and with the hunk reverted it exits cleanly. Deleting the whole `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED` block and keeping a single `memdelete(extension_wrapper)` also fixes it. Happy to open a PR for whichever form is preferred.

The Vendors plugin stopped using the deprecated class in 5.0.0 (GodotVR/godot_openxr_vendors#414), so 5.x releases are not affected. Older releases and any third-party GDExtension still on `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` are.

title: macOS: one ~25–40 ms main-thread stall ~15 s after every launch — AppKit state-restoration initial flush, although Godot's windows are not restorable
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4], both the standard and the .NET build.
- Both rendering drivers: Metal and Vulkan (MoltenVK), Forward+.

### System information

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M5 Pro (18 cores, 64 GB), built-in display at 120 Hz. Windowed, V-Sync enabled.

### Issue description

The project below does nothing except log frame intervals from one Node2D. It still drops one long frame, 24–40 ms at 120 Hz, **~15.07 s after engine start, in every launch**:
- The instant is the same within ±40 ms on the standard and .NET builds, on both drivers.
- In a game it lands mid-play as a visible hitch.

**Where the frame goes.** I timestamped the first and last `_process`, `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` / `frame_post_draw`, and an `InputEventAction` injected each frame and seen in `_input` at the next event flush.
- The whole stall falls **after `frame_post_draw` and before the next input flush**. That is between iterations, in the AppKit run loop, not in scripts, physics or rendering.
- On that frame the viewport's CPU render time is ~0.1 ms.

**What runs there.** The unified log shows, at the same instant, on the **main thread**:

```
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges]
21:26:23.263 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] Emptying for initial flush.
21:26:23.291 Godot[64184:db00db] [com.apple.AppKit:StateRestoration] -[NSPersistentUIManager flushAllChanges] finishing enqueued operations
```

- The "initial flush" took 16–28 ms on the main thread in 14 of 14 launches I matched against the log.
- Later flushes are coalesced to ~15 s and much cheaper (1–9 ms).

**Godot doesn't use this feature.**
- Every window is already opted out of restoration: `[wd.window_object setRestorable:NO]` in `platform/macos/display_server_macos.mm`.
- `GodotApplicationDelegate` answers `applicationSupportsSecureRestorableState:` with YES.
- The app-level `NSPersistentUIManager` still runs, and its first flush is the cost.

**Cause confirmed.** Turning the per-app Resume switch off through the argument domain, `-ApplePersistence NO` (AppKit echoes `ApplePersistence=NO` on stderr), removes both the StateRestoration log lines and the stall:
- With the flag: 0 of 5 launches stalled at ~15 s (Metal and Vulkan, standard and .NET).
- Without it: 19 of 20 launches stalled.

body:
### Tested versions

- Trigger found: **running the scene/project from the editor (Play, `Cmd+R` on macOS / `F6`) with more than one script tab open** — see *Steps to reproduce*.
- Same code is still unguarded on **master** (checked 2026-10-08 at `f87b8bd0a0`): `editor/script/script_text_editor.cpp:1093/1096/1098`, and `editor/script/script_text_editor.h:89` still declares `int line_number_gutter = -1;`.
- **Not** reproducible when running the project or tests without the editor (no script editor instance).
- Earlier reports: #58075 (4.0.alpha), #81135 (4.3.dev / 4.3.stable).

### System information

```
Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Unknown (27.0.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M3 - Apple M3 (8 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)
```

### Issue description

The editor's output panel prints, in a burst (hundreds of lines, roughly one per line of the affected script):

```
ERROR: scene/gui/text_edit.cpp:6981 - Index p_gutter = -1 is out of bounds (gutters.size() = 4).
```

Nothing is corrupted — the editor and the project keep working — but it floods the output and buries real errors and warnings.

**Why the argument is `-1`.** The printed line is an assertion inside the *callee* (`TextEdit::set_line_gutter_item_color()`, `scene/gui/text_edit.cpp:6981` in 4.7.2), so it points at the assertion, not at the caller. The caller is the script editor's safe-lines line-number coloring, and its argument is a member that is legitimately `-1` for any editor that is not the current tab:

1. `editor/script/script_text_editor.h:89` — `int line_number_gutter = -1;`, and `-1` is not a valid gutter index.
2. Only `ScriptTextEditor::_update_gutter_indexes()` (4.7.2: 1616) assigns a real index, and it runs from `enable_editor()` → `_enable_code_editor()` (4.7.2: 2688; master: 2684).
3. `ScriptEditor::edit()` only calls `enable_editor()` when `p_grab_focus` is true (4.7.2: 2284-2287), while the layout restore opens scripts with `edit(scr, false)` (3254/3263). So **every non-current script tab sits at `line_number_gutter == -1`** until it becomes the current tab (`_tab_changed()` → `ensure_select_current()` → `enable_editor()`).

**What reaches the consumer without a readiness check.**

- `ScriptTextEditor::_update_errors()` (4.7.2: 965, master: 1029) passes `line_number_gutter` straight to `set_line_gutt

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf]
- Not tested in other versions (only 4.7.2.stable is installed here; the behaviour is in the export-time `.tres` → `.res` conversion path, which exists in every 4.x release).

### System information

macOS 15.7.2 (Apple Silicon, arm64) - Godot v4.7.2.stable - headless export + headless `--main-pack` run (no renderer involved; Linux/X11 preset used for the PCK, same result with macOS and Web presets)

### Issue description

When a project is exported with the default `editor/export/convert_text_resources_to_binary=true`, every `@export` property declared as a `Packed*Array` **with an array-literal default** (`= []` or `= [1.0, 2.0]`) loses the value saved in the `.tres` file: loading the exported resource from the PCK returns the script default instead.

Properties declared without an initializer (`@export var b: PackedInt32Array`), with an explicit constructor (`= PackedFloat32Array()`), or as a typed Array (`@export var d: Array[int] = []`) keep their saved values. Saving the same resource with `ResourceSaver.save(res, "res://saved.res")` in editor mode and reloading it also keeps every value, so the binary resource format itself is fine; only the export-time text → binary conversion is affected. Exporting with the flag set to `false` preserves everything.

Test resource (`packed_fixture.gd` + `fixture.tres` in the MRP):

```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name PackedFixture

@export var a: PackedInt32Array = []
@export var b: PackedInt32Array
@export var c: PackedFloat32Array = PackedFloat32Array()
@export var d: Array[int] = []
@export var e: PackedFloat32Array = []
@export var f: PackedFloat32Array = [1.0, 2.0]
```

title: C# binding: a tree-owned Node's native object is disposed under its live C# wrapper on linux-arm64 headless servers — delayed SIGSEGV (si_addr 0x10) ~20–60 min into container runs, dumps available
body:
# Bug report — Godot issue template shape

## Tested versions

- Reproducible in: **4.7.2.stable.mono.official** (all six observed deaths across six separate boots; this is the only engine version the workload has run on).

## System information

- **Linux arm64** (Ubuntu 24.04 container image, `dotnet/runtime:10.0` base) inside Apple `container` CLI VMs on an **Apple Silicon** host (macOS), headless dedicated server, 4 vCPU / 3 GB cgroup limit.
- **Not reproducible** in the same build on **macOS native** (same machine, same silicon, same workload — many hours of soak, zero crashes) and so far **not reproduced** on x86_64 Linux under Proxmox LXC (a build has been running there as a deliberate contrast; previously a prior build ran 5 days continuous on it).

## Issue description

On a headless dedicated server, a tree-owned `Node` (the host's standing player node, parented under the scene) has its **native object disposed while its C# wrapper stays alive and referenced** — the wrapper is still held by a `GetNodesInGroup` snapshot and a registry. The next managed→native call on that wrapper (reading `GlobalPosition`) dereferences the dead native pointer and the process dies with **SIGSEGV at `si_addr = 0x10` (`SEGV_MAPERR`)** — a null-pointer + field-offset read, i.e. a disposed-object access, not heap corruption (two independent full-heap dumps, identical crash site both times, kernel signal notes verified).

Onset is random, ~20–60 minutes after boot — 6 crashes in 6 container boots, always the main thread, always after the workload has been ticking idle (no clients connected at death time in the cleanest case). After the crash, a `createdump` full-heap artifact confirms: no managed exception, the managed stack is short and clean (`_PhysicsProcess → enemy tick → movement-noise emission → player-group iteration`), and the heap contains exactly the expected live objects.

We audited our own code: **no managed disposal path touches these nodes** — they are only ever `QueueFree`d (deferred, tree-owned) and the container deaths happen with zero clients connected, so no peer-driven removal runs at all. The disposal itself is the mystery: something on the native/binding side retires a tree-owned node's object ~20–60 minutes in.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Export a `.NET` ARM64 Linux build of a Godot project whose headless server scene keeps a tree-owned `Node2D` registered in a node group, with a per-physics-frame workload that iterates that group and reads `Globa

title: `SceneTree` accessibility change queue grows forever without screen reader support (headless / no AccessKit)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5-stable and later (tested 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable), current `master` (4.8-dev) has the same code.
- Not reproducible in: 4.4.1-stable (no accessibility API yet).

All builds are from source without the AccessKit dependencies (the build prints "The screen reader support driver requires dependencies to be installed").

### System information

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.9), AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 8840HS. Reproduced with `--headless` and with the X11 display server; our target is Linux.

### Issue description

`SceneTree::accessibility_change_queue` (`HashSet<ObjectID>`) grows forever when the display server has no screen reader support (headless, or any build without AccessKit). Every GUI node that has ever been in the tree keeps its id in the set, including nodes that were freed long ago. Object count stays flat, only static memory grows.

Why:

- `Node::queue_accessibility_update()` inserts the node id unconditionally. `Control` calls it on entering the tree and on size changes, and so do `Label`, `Button`, containers and other GUI classes.
- The queue is consumed only by `_flush_accessibility_changes()` -> `_process_accessibility_changes()`, which runs only when `is_accessibility_enabled()` is true.
- On `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` the id is erased only when `is_accessibility_supported()` is true (`scene/main/node.cpp`).

Without screen reader support neither path runs, so nothing is ever removed.

The code was added in b106dfd4f9 "Base accessibility API." (#76829) and is unchanged on `master`.

Impact: in our UI-heavy app every scene change adds about 20–35 KB, and screens that create GUI nodes at runtime add more on top. An application that runs for weeks without a restart and changes scenes regularly keeps growing.

Possible fix: skip the insert in `SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change()` when `!is_accessibility_supported()` (nothing will ever process those entries), or do the same check in `Node::queue_accessibility_update()`.

```diff
--- a/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
+++ b/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
@@ -243,7 +243,7 @@ void SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change(const Node *p_node, bool p_remove)
 	if (p_node) {
 		if (p_remove) {
 			accessibility_change_queue.erase(p_node->get_instance_id());
-		} else {
+		} else if (is_accessibility_supported()) {
 			accessibility_change_queue.insert(p_node->get_instance_id());
 		}
 	}
```

title: Resources not removed from ResourceCache when using `set_path_cache`, causing use-after-free
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: current master, 4.7.2

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.4.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Max (Apple9) - Apple M4 Max (16 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Resources are not removed from the cache if the resource has `set_path_cache()` called on it before it's freed.

In the Resource destructor, if the current path isn't what it was originally set with in `set_path()`, the resource cache lookup fails.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/befe24c83135da887e534504874d1dcea4ed1f1c/core/io/resource.cpp#L790-L802

This can lead to a use-after-free if the resource is loaded again after it's been freed. If the memory allocated for the resource has been reused in the time between loads, this can cause segfaults.

While there are checks in `ResourceCache::get_ref()` for freed resources, the checks are both insufficient and dangerous; we're dereferencing something that we _know_ has been freed:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/befe24c83135da887e534504874d1dcea4ed1f1c/core/io/resource.cpp#L852-L871

I can produce segfaults semi-reliably using the MRP below:

### Steps to reproduce

1) Open in editor
2) Play
3) Observe crash before it finishes (If it did finish, you'll see '****Success****' in the logs)

As this relies on memory layout and allocation strategies, it won't crash every time. Using dev builds of the editor tends to more reliably produce crashes.

title: Metal: RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED underflows when textures are freed
body:
### Tested versions

Tested versions: reproducible in 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf] and in master [c9730f40a] built locally. Not reproducible with --rendering-driver vulkan (MoltenVK) on the same machine.

### System information

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.3), Apple M4, Metal 4.0, Forward+.

### Issue description

The following is my (mostly Claude's) understanding of the issue.

Our stream's OpenTelemetry gauge for Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED read about 9.2e18. That's int() clamping the float the monitor returns, which is about 1.8e19, i.e. the uint64 counter wrapped below zero. A bare project with no game code reproduces it.

- Root cause:
  - RenderingDevice adds texture_get_allocation_size() to its counter only for textures it allocates (in texture_create and shared fallbacks). On free, it subtracts that size for every texture (_free_pending_resources).
  - Every 2D texture also gets an sRGB view (rd_texture_srgb, created by texture_create_shared in texture_storage.cpp).
  - Vulkan returns 0 for a view because it empties the view's allocation.
  - Metal returns the view's MTLTexture.allocatedSize, which is the parent's size, so each texture is subtracted twice.
  - Textures imported with texture_create_from_extension have the same asymmetry: never added, but subtracted on Metal.
- Fix: in drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.cpp, texture_get_allocation_size returns 0 for views (parentTexture() != nullptr) and for imported textures, as Vulkan does. It's 2 lines.
- Side effect: with the fix, the counter's starting value is higher (about 4.8 MB vs 2.67 MB), because views freed during startup no longer get subtracted. The new number is the accurate one.
- Not tested: the imported-texture case. It needs a GDExtension or XR texture

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on macOS with Godot 4.7.2 or master, using the Metal driver (the project sets rendering_device/driver.macos="metal", Forward+).
2. Run it. It waits 10 frames, creates 20 RGBA8 256×256 ImageTextures (5,242,880 bytes in all), frees them 10 frames later, prints Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED at each step, then quits. A helper in the script prints a wrapped counter as a negative number, so the drop is easy to read.
3. Look at the output. Creating adds about 5,242,880 bytes, but freeing takes off about 10,485,000, roughly twice that. The counter ends up below where it started and wraps around (it reads as about 1.8e19 without the helper).
4. For comparison, run the same proj

title: `--headless`: passing `TEXTURE` to a function in a canvas_item shader logs a `custom_samplers` error
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.mono.official [ed1daf0bf]

### System information

Windows 10 - `--headless` (dummy renderer). Not reproducible with Vulkan Forward+ on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT.

### Issue description

If a `canvas_item` shader passes the built-in `TEXTURE` to one of its own functions, loading it in a headless run prints this error:

```
ERROR: Condition "!actions.custom_samplers.has(function->arguments[j].tex_builtin)" is true. Continuing.
   at: _dump_node_code (servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp:1329)
```

The same shader compiles without errors with a normal rendering driver. The shader is valid, and passing `TEXTURE` as an argument is the only way to use it inside a function, since functions can't access `TEXTURE` directly.

It looks like the dummy renderer's `MaterialStorage` sets up its shader compiler with empty `DefaultIdentifierActions`, so `custom_samplers` has no entry for `TEXTURE`. The RD canvas renderer sets `actions.custom_samplers["TEXTURE"] = "texture_sampler"`. The dummy renderer only compiles shaders to read their uniforms, so this is just log noise. It still shows up in every headless run, like unit tests and CI.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with this shader as `passed.gdshader`:

   ```glsl
   shader_type canvas_item;

   float alpha_at(sampler2D tex, vec2 t) {
       return texelFetch(tex, ivec2(t), 0).a;
   }

   void fragment() {
       COLOR = vec4(alpha_at(TEXTURE, UV * 32.0));
   }
   ```

2. Add this script as `check.gd`:

   ```gdscript
   extends SceneTree

   func _init():
       var material := ShaderMaterial.new()
       material.shader = load("res://passed.gdshader")
       quit()
   ```

3. Run `godot --headless --path . -s check.gd`.

The error above is printed. Running `godot --path . -s check.gd` without `--headless` prints nothing.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The two files above plus this `project.godot`:

```ini
config_version=5

[application]

config/name="headless-texture-arg-mrp"
config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7")
```

title: [Android] Two-finger scroll on touchpad / touchscreen interpreted as click-and-drag in Editor and UI
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.3+, Godot 4.4+, Godot master (commit 232e6b14ab)
- Architecture / Platform: Android (ARM64 / x86_64) on Laptop / Googlebook / Tablet with Trackpad & Keyboard

### System information

Googlebook OS - Godot v4.4 - Vulkan (Mobile) - Googlebook Laptop with Trackpad and Touchscreen

### Issue description

When using the Godot Android editor on a Googlebook laptop or tablet with a touchpad, performing a standard **two-finger scroll gesture** is interpreted by Godot as a **primary click-and-drag** (`InputEventMouseButton(BUTTON_LEFT)` followed by `InputEventMouseMotion` with `button_mask = BUTTON_MASK_LEFT`).

#### Observed Symptoms
1. **Menu items, Tree nodes, and ItemLists**: Attempting to scroll vertically through items or options reorders or drags the items instead of scrolling the container.
2. **TextEdit / CodeEdit**: Attempting to scroll through script code selects large regions of text instead of scrolling the editor view.
3. **Inspector / FileSystem docks**: Scrolling drags resources or items into other slots instead of scrolling through the property list.

#### Tested Configurations & Empirical Verification
1. **Setting: `Enable Pan and Scale Gestures` = `Off`**:
   - Result: Two-finger scroll on trackpad and touchscreen triggers click-and-drag (reordering items, selecting text).
2. **Setting: `Enable Pan and Scale Gestures` = `On` (restarted editor)**:
   - Result: Still reproducible. Exactly the same click-and-drag behavior occurs when two-finger scrolling.
3. **Screencast Demonstration**:
   - Video recording: https://youtu.be/Fm-lgbizPoM demonstrating two-finger scroll attempts resulting in click-and-drag in the editor.

#### In-Depth Root Cause Analysis
1. `onDown` in `GodotGestureHandler.kt` immediately emits touch down which is converted to an emulated `InputEventMouseButton (LEFT, pressed=true)` because `emulate_mouse_from_touch = true` is enforced in the editor (`main.cpp`).
2. `disableScrollDeadzone()` is hardcoded to `true` in `BaseGodotEditor.kt`, causing `onActionMove()` in `GodotGestureHandler.kt` to immediately forward motion without checking `pointerCount == 1`.
3. Controls enter left-drag / selection state before `GestureDetector.onScroll()` can resolve the pan gesture, and `handlePanEvent` is blocked by `!dragInProgress`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Godot Android Editor on a Googlebook laptop / tablet with touchpad.
2. Open any script in the Script Editor or a list in the Inspect

title: [macOS] SystemFont "PingFang SC" resolves to a face missing simplified Chinese glyphs such as 迟 (U+8FDF) and 远 (U+8FDC)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
Related: #82703 (fixed in 4.2 via #82712) — appears to be a regression or an uncovered case of the same face-selection problem.

### System information

macOS 15.7.4 (24G517), Apple Silicon (arm64), Godot v4.7.2.stable.official

### Issue description

On macOS, a `SystemFont` with `font_names = ["PingFang SC"]` resolves to a face that is missing some simplified Chinese glyphs. `Font.has_char()` returns `false` for 迟 (U+8FDF) and 远 (U+8FDC), and these characters render as hex-code placeholder (.notdef) boxes in Labels. Other simplified-only characters (这 边 过 还 进 连 选 设 响 门 关 乐 题 见 页) report `true` and render correctly.

PingFang SC itself definitely contains these characters — it is the macOS Simplified Chinese UI font and renders the same strings correctly in native apps. The pattern (a few simplified-only glyphs missing while most work) suggests the resolver picked a non-SC face from the PingFang font collection — the same class of issue as #82703.

Additional data points:
- Localized family name "苹方-简" shows the same holes.
- PostScript name "PingFangSC-Regular" and weight-qualified names ("PingFang SC Semibold", "PingFang SC Medium") do not resolve at all — `has_char` is false for every tested character.
- Other macOS CJK families resolve with full coverage, including at `font_weight = 600`: Hiragino Sans GB, STHeiti, Heiti SC, Songti SC.
- The `font_names` fallback chain does NOT fill the hole: `["PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB"]` still reports `has_char(迟) == false`. If per-glyph fallback across `font_names` entries is not intended behavior, it may be worth documenting; if it is intended, this is a second bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the script below as `probe.gd` and run `godot --headless -s probe.gd` in any project.
   (Equivalently, put "延迟设置" into a Label using a SystemFont with "PingFang SC" — 迟 renders as a hex placeholder box.)

```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _process(_delta: float) -> bool:
	var f := SystemFont.new()
	f.font_names = PackedStringArray(["PingFang SC"])
	for ch in ["迟", "远", "这", "边", "设", "响"]:
		print(ch, " U+%04X" % ch.unicode_at(0), " has_char=", f.has_char(ch.unicode_at(0)))
	quit()
	return true
```

Actual output:
```
迟 U+8FDF has_char=false
远 U+8FDC has_char=false
这 U+8FD9 has_char=true
边 U+8FB9 has_char=true
设 U+8BBE has_char=true
响 U+54CD has_char=true
```

Expected: `has_char` is `true` for all of them (PingFang SC contains all these

title: Loading a resource pack does not update previously loaded scripts
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7, 4.7.2, 4.6.3, 4.4

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Calling ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack() produces different results depending on whether a script has already been loaded using load() or is attached to a scene that has been loaded.

The .pck contains a modified version of the affected script with one additional variable declared.

**Case 1:** The script has not been loaded before loading the resource pack

Call ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack() to load the .pck.

The script reflects the additional variable from the resource pack.

However, the script's source_code property becomes empty. (This issue is only reproducible when the .pck file is exported with GDScript Export Mode set to Binary Tokens or Compressed binary tokens. Exporting the same .pck using Text mode works as expected.)

**Case 2:** The script has been loaded before loading the resource pack

Load the script using load() at least once, or load a scene that references it.

Call ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack() to load the .pck.

The script's additional variable is not reflected, and its source_code remains unchanged, as if the resource pack had not been loaded.

### Steps to reproduce

Download and run the project in Godot 4.7

The project contains a .pck that has a script with 2 variable declared in it. That script already exists in the project but only has 1 variable in it. This is to simulate a script "patch"

Button `Import Compressed Binary .pck` will load a .pck that was exported using the Compressed Binary GDScript Export Method
Button `Import Text .pck` will load a .pck that was exported using the Text GDScript Export Method
Button `Print Script Source` load the script file and will print the source code of one of the scripts in the console
Button `Print Script Props` load the script file and will print its properties to the console

- Press `Import Compressed Binary .pck`
- Press `Print Script Source`
- Notice that the console prints nothing
Repeat process by pressing the `Import Text .pck ` instead and notice that the source code shows up normally

title: Missing resource UIDs from `ResourceSaver`
body:
### Tested versions - Reproducible in: `v4.6.3`, `v4.7.1`, `v4.8.dev7` ### System information Godot v4.8.dev7 - Linux - Vulkan (Forward+) ### Issue description `ResourceSaver` skips uids when writing `[ext_resource]` entries for existing filesystem resource references. This is inconsistent with how a `.tscn` stores it: ```ini [ext_resource type="Resource" uid="uid://co1jtfqqh4rq0" path="res://child.tres" id="2_0xm2m"] ``` Instead we get: ```ini [ext_resource type="Resource" path="res://child.tres" id="2_0xm2m"] ```

Additional information

 #### Why this is important - Stable references - relying on `path`s is brittle and improper. - Consistency. #### Use case - I'm writing a custom `ResourceFormatSaver` - need uids in the `.tres` resources saved. #### Underlying cause `ResourceSaver` accepts a uid finder *callback* via [`set_get_resource_id_for_path`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7b12e749220a75ef87e800e080bd2732ad46854/core/io/resource_saver.cpp#L292) which is happily utilized by the [`EditorFileSystem`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7b12e749220a75ef87e800e080bd2732ad46854/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L3801). The problem arises when it's not the editor writing a `.tscn`, but a runtime writing a `.tres`, hence no uid finder callback.
--- ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a custom `extends Resource` with an `@export`. 2. Create `parent.tres` and `child.tres`. 1. Embed a reference in the parent. 4. Pass `parent.tres` to `ResourceSaver.save()` to copy it. 5. Observe no `uid` attributes written, just a loose `path="child.tres"`. Alternatively, in the MRP: 1. Run it once and inspect `output.tres`. 2. Compare it to `main.tscn` (as text). ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [resource_saver_missing_uids.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33239401/resource_saver_missing_uids.zip)

### Issue description

An app exported with the built-in signer is killed by the kernel at launch (SIGKILL, exit code 137, no output) as soon as the preset enables three or more entitlements. With one or two entitlements, or with none, the same export launches. The same bundle launches after re-signing only the main executable with Apple's codesign using the same entitlements and the hardened runtime, so the bundle contents are fine and the signature Godot writes is what the kernel rejects.

The cause is the DER encoding of the entitlements. PList::save_asn1 picks the number of length octets once, from the size of the whole document, and then every node is written with that many octets. Below 128 bytes every length is in short form and the output is valid DER. At 128 bytes or more every length is written in two-byte long form, including lengths under 128 such as the one-byte booleans. That is legal BER but not DER, which requires the shortest form. Apple's userland tools accept it, which is why codesign --verify --strict reports the app as valid, but the kernel on macOS 26 validates the blob as strict DER and treats the signature as invalid. macOS 15 accepts it (CI runners of another project pass with the same exports).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP, or any project with a macOS preset using the built-in signer.
2. In the preset enable Allow JIT Code Execution, Allow Unsigned Executable Memory and Disable Library Validation (three entitlements).
3. Export, then run Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain from a terminal: it exits with code 137 and prints nothing.
4. Disable one of the three and export again: the app runs and prints plain app started.
5. With the three enabled, re-sign the main executable with Apple's tool and run again: it launches.

codesign -d --entitlements :- --xml Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain > ent.plist
codesign -f -s - --options runtime --entitlements ent.plist Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[der_entitlements_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33236336/der_entitlements_mrp.zip)

### Issue description

In Linux/BSD, when input is being passed through Fcitx5 using Wayland's text-input protocol, `InputEvent.is_echo()` always returns false, regardless on whether key input repetition is actually occurring or not via a key being held.

This may also happen with other IMEs such as IBus, but this hasn't been tested yet.

Setting the environment variable `SDL_IM_MODULE=fcitx` corrects this. Since this is a local setting rather than something that can be packaged in a build, this can't be considered a full fix.

title: Fuzzer: several crashes when certain functions are called from a separate thread
body:
### Tested versions

e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083

### System information

Ubuntu 26.04

### Issue description

While going through the issues on github, I noticed a lot of thread related problems that are extremely difficult to reproduce and identify the actual cause.

Using a fuzzer, I called random functions on several objects from a separate thread to gather quite minimal and easy to reproduce examples, and it found quite a few problems.

There seem to be mostly 2 kinds of them:
- Methods that read/write internal members from a separate thread, asan mostly shows problems for `Vector`/`HashMap`/`LocalVector`, because those cause real crashes, but the same applies to ints/floats/bools and other builtin types, but only tsan(which is quite hard to use in bigger godot project) shows a problems with them.
- Functions like `get_world_2d()`/`get_world_3d()`, returns null in another thread because of e.g. `ERR_READ_THREAD_GUARD_V`, so a null result is then used without a null check, which crashes an engine.

If this were a single problem I would have created a PR, but since it occurs with quite big number of classes I held back (an example patch prepared, it probably does not fix everything, but it shows the quite big scope of the change, which consists a lot of fairly simple edits).

I wondered how this could be fixed globally, the way Rust does it, by preventing incorrect usage at compile time. However, given my limited skills with advanced C++ and the limitations of C++ itself, which probably makes this impossible, I could not come up with anything sensible apart from ad-hoc adding a lot of mutexes to the functions.

Patch, which fixes most of these problems - [all_fixes.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33218142/all_fixes.patch)

|---|---|

title: OS.read_buffer_from_stdin() returns the whole buffer filled with old memory on Windows
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]

### System information

Windows 11 build 26200, Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] (running --headless)

### Issue description

I'm working on a small headless tool for my game where a python script plays the game by sending moves over stdin.

`read_string_from_stdin` strips the newlines, so a read that only got a `\n` comes back as `""`, same as when the pipe closes. The docs say to use `read_buffer_from_stdin` for unprocessed data, so I switched to it, and noticed a strange potential bug?

It seems that, at least on Windows, `read_buffer_from_stdin` always hands back the full `buffer_size`, no matter how much was actually read, and whatever comes after the data is old memory.

In my case I sent the text/bytes `AB\n`, calling it like this (this is the MRP's script; the `0xAA` part is only there to see whether old memory shows up):

```gdscript
print("stdin type: %d" % OS.get_stdin_type())
var canary := PackedByteArray()
canary.resize(64)
canary.fill(0xAA)
canary = PackedByteArray() # freed right before the reads
for i in 4:
	var got := OS.read_buffer_from_stdin(64)
	print("read %d: size %d: %s" % [i + 1, got.size(), got.hex_encode()])
	if got.is_empty():
		break

```

and got 64 bytes back.

So to recap:

**What I send** (3 bytes through a pipe):

```
41 42 0a                      "AB\n"

```

**What I expect** (what the docs describe, and what the Linux/macOS code does):

```
read 1 -> 3 bytes:   41 42 0a
read 2 -> 0 bytes    (pipe closed)

```

**What I get on Windows:**

```
read 1 -> 64 bytes:  41 42 0a 00 74 00 00 00 64 00 00 00 69 00 00 00 6e 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 74 00 00 00 79 00 00 00 70 00 00 00 65 00 00 00 3a 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 33 00 00 00 0a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
read 2 -> 0 bytes

```

Which does show my `AB\n`... but then a whole bunch of data I never asked for. The 64-byte size happens every single time I've tried it; what's in the extra 61 bytes varies.

Mostly it's zeros, but in one run it was the line my script printed just before the read. Read 4 bytes at a time (UTF-32, which is how Godot stores a String), `74 00 00 00` is `t`, `64 00 00 00` is `d`, and so on, spelling `tdin type: 3\n`, with the `s` overwritten by my `AB\n`.

And it gets worse if `stdin` is a file.  
After EOF it never returns an empty array and just keeps giving back 64 bytes, so essentially the expectation of "read until empty" never happens and the loop never ends. The docs say a

title: Use-after-free crash when an embedded Window is freed after a root viewport resize (deferred Viewport::_sub_window_update with a raw Window*)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 
- 4.8.dev7 [c971f93e7]
- 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf]
- 4.6.stable [89cea1439]

Official Linux builds crash in 10 of 10 runs (20 of 20 on 4.6). Also reproducible in a 4.6.stable source build with use_asan=yes, which reports a heap-use-after-free.

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic) - Godot v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] - headless (--headless, dummy rendering driver) - AMD Ryzen 9 9900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads)

### Issue description

The engine segfaults on the next frame when an embedded subwindow is freed with `free()` after the root viewport's size or `content_scale_factor` changed earlier in the same frame. The expected behavior is no crash: the pending redraw of a freed subwindow should be skipped.

**Cause:** `Viewport::update_canvas_items()` (called from `Viewport::_set_size()`) queues a deferred call for each embedded subwindow with a **raw `Window *`** argument:

```cpp
for (Viewport::SubWindow w : gui.sub_windows) {
	if (w.window && !w.pending_window_update) {
		w.pending_window_update = true;
		w.window->_update_viewport_size();
		callable_mp(this, &Viewport::_sub_window_update).call_deferred(w.window);
	}
}
```

When the message queue flushes, `call_with_variant_args` validates the argument through `VariantObjectClassChecker<Window *>::check()` (`core/variant/binder_common.h:150`). That converts the `Variant` to an `Object *` without checking its `ObjectID`, then calls `Object::cast_to<Window>()`. The cast makes a virtual `is_class_ptr()` call on the freed object. This happens before `_sub_window_update()` runs, so the `index == -1` early return added for #100613 doesn't help. That check handles a subwindow that was *closed*, not one that was *freed*.

In official builds the crash is often intermittent, depending on whether the allocator has reused the freed memory by the time the queue flushes. We hit it in a headless test suite: a test changed the UI scale while a `ConfirmationDialog` was open, then freed the scene, and the crash surfaced dozens of tests later at the first `await process_frame`. With AddressSanitizer it's deterministic:

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x51f000064a90 ...
READ of size 8 at 0x51f000064a90 thread T0
    #0 in bool Object::derives_from<Window, Object>() const core/object/object.h:1067
    #1 in Window* Object::cast_to<Window>(Object*) core/object/object.h:846
    #2 in VariantObjectClassChecker<Window*>::check
[truncated]

title: Shader baker: export logs "Failed loading resource" errors for CSV translation files
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable (Arch Linux package, ed1daf0bf). Not reproducible with the shader baker disabled.

### System information

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.5), Forward+, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070

### Issue description

With `shader_baker/enabled=true` in an export preset, exporting a project that has a CSV translation logs three errors:

```
ERROR: Resource file not found:  (expected type: Translation)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://strings.csv.
ERROR: Condition "res.is_null()" is true. Returning: p_path
```

The export still succeeds and the `.translation` file is packed and loads in game, so the errors seem harmless. With the shader baker disabled, the same export logs nothing.

It looks like enabling the baker adds a resource customization plugin. `EditorExportPlatform::_export_customize()` is then called with the imported file's *source* path (`res://strings.csv`) and tries to `ResourceLoader::load()` it. The CSV translation importer writes one file per locale, so its `.import` has no single `path=` remap, and the load fails. Possibly related: #110931.

Expected: no errors, e.g. customization skips imports that have no single resource path, as it does for `keep` and `skip` importers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with a translation CSV (`strings.csv`, below), let it import, and add `res://strings.en.translation` to Localization > Translations.
2. Add a Linux export preset with **Shader Baker** enabled.
3. Export: `godot --path . --export-release Linux build/repro.x86_64` (not headless, since the baker needs a rendering device).
4. The three errors above appear. Disable Shader Baker and export again: no errors.

title: Android (Compatibility, Mali): native memory grows without end when 3D MSAA is on and scaling_3d_scale < 1.0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (official export templates)

### System information

Google Pixel 9 Pro XL (Tensor G4, Mali GPU), Android 17 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Compatibility renderer (OpenGL ES 3), debug export

### Issue description

On Android with the Compatibility renderer, the app's native memory grows steadily and without end (about 4.5-6.4 MB per second) when **both** of these are set:
- `Viewport.msaa_3d` is on (tested with `MSAA_2X`), and
- `Viewport.scaling_3d_scale` is below 1.0 (tested with 0.53 and 0.5).

Each setting alone is flat. Godot's own memory counters (`OS.get_static_memory_usage()`, `MEMORY_STATIC`, `RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED`) stay flat while the process native heap climbs, so the growth seems to be outside Godot's allocator: driver side, or a GL object Godot does not count (perhaps a multisample/resolve buffer re-created every frame and never freed).

Minimal project below, measured on the same phone with `adb shell dumpsys meminfo <package>`:

| MRP build | Native Heap | TOTAL PSS | Godot static / video memory (own counters) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSAA 2x, scale 0.53 | 153 MB at 10 s -> 441 MB at 55 s (~6.4 MB/s, linear) | 479 -> 765 MB | flat 33.4 MB / 45.6 MB |
| MSAA off, scale 0.53 | 62.9 MB at 10 s -> 56.6 MB at 180 s (flat) | 393 -> 379 MB | flat 34.3 MB / 45.6 MB |

In our full game (3 minutes per run, one change per run):

| MSAA 3D | 3D scale | Native memory over 3 min |
|---|---|---|
| 2x | 0.53 | grows ~4.5 MB/s, no plateau |
| off | 0.53 | flat, ~217 MB |
| 2x | 1.0 | flat, ~227 MB |
| 2x | 0.5 | grows (same slope) |

The same game build on Windows (same renderer) is flat. Workaround: turn MSAA off whenever `scaling_3d_scale < 1.0`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new 3D project with the Compatibility renderer, with one camera and a few meshes that move every frame (the MRP below).
2. At start: `get_viewport().msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_2X` and `get_viewport().scaling_3d_scale = 0.53`.
3. Export to Android (debug) and run it on a Mali-GPU phone.
4. Every 10 s, run `adb shell dumpsys meminfo <package>`: Native Heap and TOTAL PSS climb steadily.

title: Exporting a C# resource and assigning it from GDScript gives an error
body:
### Tested versions

- Not reproducible in 4.8.dev2 and earlier
- Reproducible on 4.8.dev3 and later

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev3.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7688) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12600KF (16 threads) - 31.81 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Under specific circumstances, trying to assign a C# Resource (class created and used in C#) from GDScript will give the `Cannot assign a new value to a constant.` error.
For this error to happen, the C# class must inherit from `Resource` (`RefCounted`, `GodotObject` and `Node` don't give this error), must have the `[GlobalClass]` attribute, and when defined in another class, must have `[Export]`

This is honestly really confusing to describe, so I'll just give a small code example:
```cs
// res://MyResource.cs
[GlobalClass] // Must be a [GlobalClass] for the error to happen
public partial class MyResource : Resource { } // Must be a Resource for the error to happen

// res://MyOtherClass.cs
[GlobalClass]
public partial class MyOtherClass : Node // The type this class inherits from doesn't matter
{
    [Export] public MyResource MyRes; // Must have [Export] for the error to happen
}
```
```gdscript
extends Node
func _ready():
   var test := MyOtherClass.new()
   test.MyRes = null # Cannot assign a new value to a constant.
   test.MyRes = MyResource.new() # Cannot assign a new value to a constant.
```

### Steps to reproduce

I've kind of describe them above, and I've also included an MRP below, which should hopefully clear things up more.
When making a change to the C# side of the MRP, don't forget to re-compile and to save the GDScript script again.
Sometimes, the script editor might not update properly and won't show the error, but the Output tab will always have the error if it's there. You can always save the script to make the error show up in the Output tab.

title: Mobile renderer: GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D is never cleared between updates

### Tested Versions

4.7.2.stable

### System information

Windows 11, RTX 4080 Laptop / Android (Samsung S25 FE), Mobile renderer (Vulkan)

### Issue description

When using the Mobile renderer, moving `GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D` (e.g. with `follow_camera_enabled = true`) leaves trails behind obstacles. It seems the heightfield texture is never cleared between updates, causing previous collision data to smear along movement.

This does not happen in Forward+.

It looks like the fix from #102133 was applied to `render_forward_clustered.cpp`, but the Mobile equivalent in `render_forward_mobile.cpp` is missing `RD::DRAW_CLEAR_ALL`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the attached MRP with the Mobile renderer.
2. Observe particles landing in mid-air on the smeared trail left behind by the bump.
3. Switch to Forward+ to see correct behavior.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[heightfield_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33170576/heightfield_mrp.zip)

title: Audio mix thread can read freed AudioStreamPlaybackBusDetails when it is descheduled (use after free in _mix_step)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
- The code involved is unchanged on master.

### System information

macOS 26.5.2, Apple M4 Pro (12 cores), headless (`--headless`, so the Dummy audio driver)

### Issue description

The audio mix thread can read an `AudioStreamPlaybackBusDetails` after the main thread has freed it, and crash with EXC_BAD_ACCESS.

`AudioServer::set_playback_bus_volumes_linear()` swaps in new bus details and puts the old ones in `bus_details_graveyard`. `_cleanup_lists()`, called from `AudioServer::update()` on the main thread, moves them to `bus_details_graveyard_frame_old` and deletes them one update later. So the old details live for two main loop iterations after the swap.

`_mix_step()` on the mix thread loads the pointer with `playback->bus_details.load()` and then copies the struct (`AudioStreamPlaybackBusDetails bus_details = *bus_details_ptr;`), which copies its `StringName`s, then calls `thread_find_bus_index()` on them. Nothing ties the deletion to the mix thread being done with the pointer: `_cleanup_lists()` does not take the driver lock, and the two-update delay is only a timing assumption.

When the mix thread is descheduled between the load and the copy for longer than two main loop iterations (about 16 ms at 120 frames a second), it reads freed memory. `AudioStreamPlayer2D` updates its bus volumes as it pans, so with players or the camera moving, swaps are constant.

We hit it in automated headless test runs on a busy machine: about 1 in 4 runs crashed when the CPU was oversubscribed, and never on an idle machine. All crash reports show the same stack on an unnamed (non WorkerThreadPool) thread:

```
Godot +0x3e5c304   <- return into AudioServer::_mix_step, right after the call for thread_find_bus_index / bus_map lookup
Godot +0x3e5c304
Godot +0x3e5a418   <- likely AudioServer::_driver_process
Godot +0x3e56c50   <- likely AudioDriverDummy::thread_func (a lock, process, unlock loop)
Godot +0x1a5a7f8   <- Thread::callback
_pthread_start
```

The official macOS build has no symbols, so the frame names above are my reading of the disassembly, not symbolicated. The crashing function references the strings `servers/audio/audio_server.cpp`, `thread_get_channel_mix_buffer`, `p_bus` and `buses.size()`, and the faulting call sits right after the bus details copy, on `bus_map` (`this + 0x210`) with a `StringName` from the copied details.

Godot's own crash handler then prints `ERROR: /root: The

title: TreeItem child cache becomes inconsistent after move_before() followed by indexed insertion
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in official builds:
- 4.6.stable.official.89cea1439
- 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf

Regression range unknown. Development builds have not been tested.

### System information

macOS 15.6.1, ARM64. Reproduced using headless execution.

### Issue description

Reordering children of a native `TreeItem` with `move_before()`, then inserting children at indices `0` and `2`, produces an out-of-bounds error and an incorrect child count.

**Expected:** Five children, with `get_child_count()` returning `5`, and no errors.

**Actual:** `get_child_count()` returns `1`, although traversing the children using `get_first_child()` and `get_next()` finds all five.

Relevant output:

```text
ERROR: Index p_pos = 2 is out of bounds (count + 1 = 2).
   at: insert (./core/templates/local_vector.h:275)
   GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
       [0] _initialize (res://repro.gd:15)
Children: 1
Actual item: first
Actual item: a
Actual item: inserted
Actual item: c
Actual item: b
```

The reproduction uses only native `Tree` and `TreeItem` APIs. No plugins, GDExtensions, assets, or custom engine modifications are involved.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Extract the attached project.
2. From its directory, run the following command, replacing `godot` with the executable path if necessary:

   ```sh
   godot --headless --path . --script res://repro.gd
   ```

title: Android: releasing the stylus side button during a drag ends the drag, and the rest of the stroke is lost
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable: observed in Pixelorama 1.2.3's official Android build, which uses the official 4.7.2 Android export template.
- The relevant code is unchanged on master (c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f).
- The minimal project below logs the same events. I have not yet run it as a separate app on the device.

### System information

Android 14 – XPPen Magic Note Pad (model MNP1095), Mali-G57 MC2, Compatibility renderer (OpenGL ES 3.2). Stylus: XPPen X3 Pro Pencil 2 (EMR, one side button).

### Issue description

When the pen's side button is released while the pen is still touching the screen and moving, Godot sends a mouse button release at that moment, and after that no events at all arrive until the pen is lifted. The rest of the stroke is lost.

Raw pen data (`getevent`) for one stroke: tip down for about 7 seconds, side button pressed after 1.2 s and released after 3.3 s. Godot reports the release at 3.3 s and nothing for the remaining 3.8 s.

I expected releasing the side button to only change the button state of the following motion events, and the drag to continue until the pen is lifted.

**Cause, as far as I can tell:** Android delivers `ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE` through `onGenericMotionEvent` (it is not a touch event). `GodotGestureHandler.onActionUp` handles it like `ACTION_UP` while a drag is in progress:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/input/GodotGestureHandler.kt#L154-L158

The native side then marks the pointer as released (`_release_mouse_event_info`), so the following `ACTION_MOVE` events are dropped because `mouse_event_info.valid` is false.

As a workaround I set a `View.OnGenericMotionListener` on Godot's view (through `JavaClassWrapper.create_sam_callback`) that swallows stylus `ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS` and `ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE`. With that, the drag continues correctly after the button is released.

### Steps to reproduce

title: Android: dragging with the stylus side button held sometimes becomes a magnify gesture with no motion events
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable: observed in Pixelorama 1.2.3's official Android build, which uses the official 4.7.2 Android export template.
- The relevant code is unchanged on master (c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f).
- The minimal project below logs the same events. I have not yet run it as a separate app on the device.

### System information

Android 14 – XPPen Magic Note Pad (model MNP1095), Mali-G57 MC2, Compatibility renderer (OpenGL ES 3.2). Stylus: XPPen X3 Pro Pencil 2 (EMR, one side button).

### Issue description

With `input_devices/pointing/android/enable_pan_and_scale_gestures` enabled, holding the stylus side button and then dragging on the screen sometimes produces only `InputEventMagnifyGesture` events and no `InputEventMouseMotion` at all. In my measurements this happened in 18 of 66 strokes. For the whole stroke there are no positions, so a drawing app cannot draw, and the app zooms instead.

I expected a stylus drag to always deliver motion events. The stylus quick-scale gesture is useful in some apps, but it should not replace motion events, or it should be possible to turn it off.

**Cause, as far as I can tell:** `GodotInputHandler` enables stylus scaling on its `ScaleGestureDetector`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/input/GodotInputHandler.java#L120

Android then treats "stylus button held + drag" as a quick-scale gesture. Whether drawing or scaling wins depends on timing: `GodotGestureHandler.onScaleBegin` refuses to start while a drag is in progress, and `onScroll` stops sending motion while a scale is in progress. When scaling wins, the drag never gets motion events.

Calling `setStylusScaleEnabled(false)` on that detector (I did it from GDScript through `JavaClassWrapper` and reflection as a workaround) makes every stroke deliver motion events, and two-finger pinch still works.

Related: #78059 (S Pen and long-press right-click).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Export the MRP to an Android device with a stylus that has a side button.
2. About 20 times: hold the side button, then touch the screen and drag.
3. Some strokes show `MagnifyGesture factor=...` lines and no `MouseMotion` lines in the log.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

title: Android: stylus side button is reported as MouseButton NONE (index 0) with an empty button mask
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable: observed in Pixelorama 1.2.3's official Android build, which uses the official 4.7.2 Android export template.
- The relevant code is unchanged on master (c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f).
- The minimal project below logs the same events. I have not yet run it as a separate app on the device.

### System information

Android 14 – XPPen Magic Note Pad (model MNP1095), Mali-G57 MC2, Compatibility renderer (OpenGL ES 3.2). Stylus: XPPen X3 Pro Pencil 2 (EMR, one side button).

### Issue description

When the pen touches the screen while its side button is held, Godot reports:

- an `InputEventMouseButton` with `button_index = 0` (`MOUSE_BUTTON_NONE`), `pressed = true`, `button_mask = 0`,
- `InputEventMouseMotion` events with `button_mask = 0` even though the pen is touching (`pressure > 0`),
- a matching `button_index = 0` release when the pen lifts.

Each of these presses and releases also logs `ERROR: Condition "button == MouseButton::NONE" is true. Returning: MouseButtonMask::NONE` from `mouse_button_to_mask`.

So a script cannot tell "touching with the side button held" apart from hovering, apart from checking pressure. Drawing apps built with Godot (I ran into this with Pixelorama) ignore the touch completely.

I expected the side button to be reported as a usable button, for example `MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT` (as on desktop with many tablet drivers), or at least not as `NONE` with an empty mask.

The pen hardware itself is fine: `getevent` on the device shows `BTN_TOUCH` and `BTN_STYLUS` correctly.

**Cause, as far as I can tell:** Android reports the side button as `BUTTON_STYLUS_PRIMARY` in `MotionEvent.getButtonState()`. In `GodotInputHandler.handleMouseEvent`, `BUTTON_PRIMARY` is only added when the button state is 0:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c016f22009aa773f0b2e6fce72baec168746491f/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/input/GodotInputHandler.java#L675-L680

With the side button held, the state is `BUTTON_STYLUS_PRIMARY` (not 0), so no primary bit is added, and `AndroidInputHandler::_android_button_mask_to_godot_button_mask` has no mapping for the stylus buttons, so the mask ends up empty and the pressed button becomes `NONE`.

Related: stylus button support was left for a follow-up in #80644 (pressure and tilt support), and godotengine/godot-proposals#6659 proposes stylus button support in general. #116740 shows the same error message, triggered by a U

title: Mono Array.Insert implementation is not equivalent to GDScript implementation
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.7.stable.mono.official [5b4e0cb0f] and probably in every build ever

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.31041.1004) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.15 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

C# Array.Insert implementation doesn't have the ability to insert with negative indexes.

```gdscript
var a = []
	a.insert(0, 1) # [1]
	a.insert(1, 2); # [1, 2]
	a.insert(-1, 3); # [1, 3, 2]
	print(a);
```

```c#
var arr = new Array();
        arr.Insert(0, 1); // [1]
        arr.Insert(1, 2); // [1, 2]
        arr.Insert(-1, 3); // ArgumentOutOfRangeException
        GD.Print(arr);
```

As well as the current C# Array.Insert method documentation doesn't describe itself correctly. [This line](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Array.cs#L826) fails to mention that passing Array.Count as the position is actually supported.

Expected behaviour:
Array.Insert should support negative indexes. 

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
var a = []
	a.insert(0, 1)
	a.insert(1, 2);
	a.insert(-1, 3);
	print(a);
```

```C#
var arr = new Array();
        arr.Insert(0, 1);
        arr.Insert(1, 2);

title: Crash (SIGSEGV, stack exhaustion) in `VariantParser::parse` when loading a config/resource file with deeply nested containers — no recursion depth limit
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.x master `e2b42469291c6889f93ad83debb5d24f607d26e3` (2026-09-21) — release and ASan builds, 6/6 attempts SIGSEGV.
- The recursive-descent parser `core/variant/variant_parser.cpp` has no depth counter; the defect is structural (not a recent regression). Not tested on tagged 4.7.2-stable binaries, but the parser code path is unchanged by inspection.

### System information

Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 22.04 base); Godot built from source with scons (`platform=linuxbsd target=editor`, gcc 11.4; separate ASan build with `-fsanitize=address`). Crash occurs in `--headless` mode (no GPU involved).

### Issue description

`VariantParser` (the shared recursive-descent parser behind `ConfigFile`
(.cfg/.tres/.tscn) and binary resource text forms) recurses
`parse_value() → parse_array()/parse_dictionary() → parse_value()` once per
nesting level with **no depth limit**. A config file containing ~300k nested
`[` characters exhausts the call stack and crashes the process:

```
(godot --headless --script load_cfg.gd with CFG=poc_nested.cfg) → SIGSEGV, exit 139
```

Both release and ASan builds crash identically (stack exhaustion). A control
file with a shallow container parses fine (`load err=0`).

For contrast, the **GDScript runtime has a recursion-depth guard** for the same
class of expression nesting (`GDScriptParser` / VM recursion limits) — the
VariantParser path missed that protection, so this reads as a missed
hardening rather than by-design behaviour.

Beyond the crash itself: the parser is reachable from project/resource loading,
so a malicious project or asset file obtained from a third party (e.g. a
shared demo/template) crashes the editor or any godot-based tool that loads it.

### Steps to reproduce

**1. generate the deeply nested config (one line, ~600 KB):**

```bash
python3 -c "open('poc_nested.cfg','wb').write(b'key=' + b'[' * 300000)"
```

**2. save the loader script as `load_cfg.gd`:**

```gdscript
extends SceneTree
func _init():
	var cf = ConfigFile.new()
	var err = cf.load(OS.get_environment("CFG"))
	print("load err=", err)
	quit(0)
```

**3. run (attack vs control):**

```bash
# control: shallow file, parses cleanly
printf 'key=[1, 2]\n' > ctrl_plain.cfg
CFG=ctrl_plain.cfg godot --headless --script load_cfg.gd
# → load err=0, exit 0

# attack: 300k nesting
CFG=poc_nested.cfg godot --headless --script load_cfg.gd
# → Segmentation fault (exit 139), both release and ASan builds, 6/6 runs
```

The same crash is reacha

title: Dummy renderer: `texture_owner` is not thread-safe; threaded texture loads under `--headless` intermittently error "Parameter "t" is null"
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]
- Not tested on other versions.

### System information

macOS 26.6 (arm64, Apple M5 Max), `--headless` (dummy rendering server), official release binary.

### Issue description

With `--headless`, loading imported `Texture2D` resources through `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request()` while the main thread creates other texture RIDs intermittently prints:

```
ERROR: Parameter "t" is null.
   at: texture_2d_initialize (./servers/rendering/dummy/storage/texture_storage.h:85)
```

The dummy `TextureStorage` declares its owner as

```cpp
mutable RID_PtrOwner<DummyTexture> texture_owner;
```

in `servers/rendering/dummy/storage/texture_storage.h`, which is not thread-safe, but the resource loader allocates and initializes textures on worker threads while the main thread can allocate and free texture RIDs at the same time. The race corrupts the owner, and `texture_2d_initialize()` then finds no texture for the RID it was just handed.

Changing the declaration to the thread-safe form removes the error:

```cpp
mutable RID_PtrOwner<DummyTexture, true> texture_owner;
```

Results with the minimal project below, run in a loop on the same machine (a run counts when stderr contains `Parameter "t" is null`):

| Binary | Runs with the error |
|---|---|
| official 4.7.1.stable | 8 of 232 |
| same source with the one-line change | 0 of 200 |

This only affects the dummy (headless) renderer; other renderers' texture owners are not involved.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project whose `project.godot` contains only `config_version=5`, plus six PNG files `a.png` … `f.png` (any content, for example 2048×1024 noise; a generator is below).
2. Import once: `godot --headless --path . --import`
3. Save the script below as `repro.gd` and run it about 100 times:
   `godot --headless --path . --script repro.gd`
4. Count the runs whose stderr contains `Parameter "t" is null`.

`repro.gd`:

```gdscript
extends SceneTree

const PATHS := ["res://a.png", "res://b.png", "res://c.png", "res://d.png", "res://e.png", "res://f.png"]

func _initialize() -> void:
	call_deferred("_run")

func _run() -> void:
	for path in PATHS:
		ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(path, "Texture2D")
	var pending := PATHS.duplicate()
	var keep: Array = []
	while not pending.is_empty():
		keep.clear()
		for i in 16: # main-thread RID churn while the workers create textures
			var g := GradientTexture2D.new()
			g.width = 32
			g.heigh
[truncated]
