title: GDScript: use-after-free in GDScript::_create_instance when _init() fails (crash after new() with missing arguments)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (Linux x86_64, official editor binary).
  Also reproducible in a custom build of the same commit (ed1daf0bf) with debug_symbols=yes, where the
  backtrace below comes from.
- Fixed by reordering two statements (patch below): 0 crashes in a build of ed1daf0bf with the patch.
- master: not run, but the code in modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp (_create_instance, both failure paths)
  is identical to 4.7.2 today (03.10.2026), so it is likely affected.
- Windows 4.7.2.stable: the same failure path (a failed new() on a script where _init needs an
  argument) ran without crashing in our project's test. The bug is a use-after-free, so whether
  it crashes depends on the allocator. The MRP hasn't been run on Windows.
- Earlier versions: not tested.

### System information

Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 base, kernel 6.8.0-139-generic, glibc 2.39) - Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] - reproduced with --headless (no rendering); also seen with the X11/GLX opengl3 renderer - NVIDIA GeForce GT 650M (nvidia 470.256.02) - Intel Core i7-3615QM CPU @ 2.30GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

Calling `new()` on a GDScript where `_init()` requires an argument, without passing it, should print
an error and return `null`. On Linux the engine frequently segfaults instead, inside the failed
`new()` call. It happens with `script.new()`, `script.callv("new", [])` and
`Callable(script, "new").call()`, with no GDExtension or plugins involved.

On both failure paths of `GDScript::_create_instance` (modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp, the
`_super_implicit_constructor` failure and the `_init` failure), the cleanup runs in this order:

```cpp
instance->script = Ref<GDScript>();
instance->owner->set_script_instance(nullptr);   // deletes instance
{
    MutexLock lock(GDScriptLanguage::singleton->mutex);
    instances.remove(&instance->script_instance_list);   // reads and writes the freed instance
}
```

`set_script_instance()` calls `memdelete()` on the current script instance, so the
`GDScriptInstance` is already freed when `instances.remove(&instance->script_instance_list)` reads
and writes its `SelfList` node. Clearing `instance->script` first stops `~GDScriptInstance` from
unlinking the node itself, so the remove can't be skipped either. Whether it crashes depends on
whether the freed block has been reused yet. 

Suggested fix: unlink the instance from `instances` before `set_script_instance(nullptr)` frees it
[truncated]

title: Metal: push constants re-applied by compute_list_add_barrier() overwrite the next pipeline's uniform set (GPU page fault, timeout waiting for fence freeze)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.dev7.official [c971f93e7]
- Not tested, but the same code path exists in 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable and current master (e7cfa294a0). See "Cause" below.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Unknown (27.0.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

On Metal, if `compute_list_add_barrier()` is followed by a dispatch of a pipeline that has **no** push constants, that pipeline's uniform set gets overwritten. The overwrite happens at the Metal buffer index where the *previous* pipeline kept its push constants. The other drivers are not affected, because push constants there do not share slots with descriptor sets.

In the MRP this only produces a wrong result. In a real project the overwritten set held 20 sampled textures (a 320-byte argument buffer). The shader then read texture handles out of the 16 bytes of push constant data, which caused `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`. After that, Metal ignores every further command buffer (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored`), and the engine freezes with an endless stream of:

```
ERROR: timeout waiting for fence
   at: wait (drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal3.cpp:58)
```

The freeze happened at random, but the overwrite happened on every frame.

#### Cause

1. `RenderingDevice::compute_list_add_barrier()` ends the compute list, begins a new one, and re-records the previous pipeline, uniform sets **and push constants** ([rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216)).
2. During replay, `MDCommandBufferBase::encode_push_constant_data()` stores the data, sets `push_constant_binding` to the push constant index of the *previous* shader (index 1 here, because that shader only has set 0), and sets `DIRTY_PUSH` ([metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728)).
3. The caller binds a different pipeline. `MDCommandBuffer::bind_pipeline()` marks the pipeline and the uniform sets dirty, but leaves `DIRTY_PUSH` and `push_constant_binding` untouched ([metal3_objects.cpp#L431-L437](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e7
[truncated]

### Issue description

When editing the  Name  of a custom data entry inside TileSet's Custom Data Layer, the field name shown in the left tile paint panel will not refresh automatically and keeps showing the old name.
However, if you modify the  Type  of the same entry (for example, switch int to string and revert it), the name in the paint panel will update to the new name immediately.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create or open a TileSet and navigate to Custom Data Layer.
2. Add a custom data entry: set  Name=hu ,  Type=int .
3. Select a tile and fill a value for this custom property in the paint panel.
4. Go back to Custom Data Layer and change the entry's  Name  to  test .
5. Check the left-side tile paint panel.

Result: The field label still shows the old name  hu , not  test .

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or open a TileSet and navigate to Custom Data Layer.
2. Add a custom data entry: set  Name=hu ,  Type=int .
3. Select a tile and fill a value for this custom property in the paint panel.
4. Go back to Custom Data Layer and change the entry's  Name  to  test .
5. Check the left-side tile paint panel.

Result: The field label still shows the old name  hu , not  test .

6. Modify the  Type  of this entry (int → string).

Result: The tile paint panel refreshes, and the label updates to  test .

Expected behavior

Changing the  Name  of a custom data entry should automatically sync and update the label in the tile paint panel, without needing to modify the  Type .

Actual behavior

- Changing only  Name : UI label in paint panel stays at old name, no refresh.
- Changing  Type  (any type switch): triggers full UI refresh, then the new name appears.

Environment

- Godot version: 4.7 stable
- OS: Windows

Additional information

- Reading and writing the custom data value works correctly. This bug only affects the UI label display.
- Re-selecting tiles or switching panels cannot trigger the name refresh. Only changing Type triggers the refresh.

Workaround

As a temporary solution, modify the property Type and revert it after renaming to force the UI to refresh.

title: [XR] Evaluating bounded spatial container experiences running at lower framerates
body:
[OpenXR Spatial Containers](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XR_EXT_spatial_container) are a new cross-platform spatial windowing API which provides applications the ability to display XR content within bounded or immersive system-managed spaces.

Typically, applications running in fully immersive XR need to run at least at 72fps to provide a pleasant, non-nauseating experience to the user given how much of the user's field of view they occupy.

When running in a bounded spatial container however, XR applications take a much smaller field of view, not dissimilar to non-XR, regular flat applications. As such the minimum threshold for a good framerate can be much lower than 72fps.

In this issue I document some of the Godot spatial container samples running at various framerates below 72fps, and describe my (subjective) experience when interacting with them.

title: Audio output is floor-truncated to 16 bits without dither, including on drivers that hand the OS float (WASAPI, Web)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable [a13da4feb] (Linux, and a Web export), 4.7.stable [5b4e0cb0f] (macOS).
- The conversion code is the same in 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf] and on master at [e7cfa294a] (read, not built).
- Not a regression: the same int32 packing and `>> 16` are in 3.0.stable and 4.0.stable (read, not run).

### System information

Measured on three systems, all with the official builds:  - **Linux:** Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] - Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64 (headless container, no GPU, `--display-driver headless`) - audio driver: PulseAudio (server 16.1) - output device: null sink, float32le, 2 ch, 48000 Hz - mix rate 48000 Hz - **macOS:** Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] - macOS 15.7.9 (24G830) - MacBook Air (15-inch, M2), 8 GB (`--display-driver headless`) - audio driver: CoreAudio - output device: Pro Tools Audio Bridge 2-B (a virtual loopback device), float32, 2 ch, 48000 Hz - mix rate 48000 Hz - **Web:** export from Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] with the official templates, thread support on - Chromium 141.0.7390.37, headless, on the Linux system above (software-rendered WebGL 2) - audio driver: AudioWorklet - AudioContext at 48000 Hz  Not measured: Windows (WASAPI, XAudio2), Android (OpenSL ES), Linux ALSA. Those are read from the source.

### Issue description

The mixer works in float. On the way to the device the signal is quantized twice, and neither step rounds or dithers.

1. `AudioServer::_driver_process()` clamps each sample, multiplies it by `(1 << 20) - 1`, truncates toward zero and shifts the magnitude left by 11. The result is a 21-bit value in an `int32_t`:
   https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/servers/audio/audio_server.cpp#L96-L105
2. Each output driver then keeps the top 16 bits with an arithmetic `>> 16`, which is floor (rounding toward −∞):
   - CoreAudio (macOS, iOS, visionOS), 16-bit signed-integer stream format: [L146-L151](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/coreaudio/audio_driver_coreaudio.mm#L146-L151), [L217](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/coreaudio/audio_driver_coreaudio.mm#L217)
   - PulseAudio, `PA_SAMPLE_S16LE`: [L234](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/pulseaudio/audio_driver_pulseaudio.cpp#L234), [L426](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e

The window's close button (X) OR using Alt+F4

body:
### Tested versions

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS 26.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 threads) - 15.32 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Imported GLBs (and possibly other assets) use a stale cached imported scene even after automatic and manual reimports under certain conditions (described below).

NOTE: This does not occur when using .blend files directly, only with exported .glb/.gltf scenes.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/156b255d-ba5f-4331-997b-49bb9286e519

### Steps to reproduce

This is basically a description of the video above.

1. Open MRP and test.tscn.
2. Export the test cube .blend as a glb into the mrp resources folder.
3. Drag into the scene to ensure import is correct (optional).
4. Delete the instance you added in step 3 from test.tscn so no instance is open (this is important).
5. In Blender, make some noticeable change and re-export, overwriting the glb (in the video I just scaled on the x axis and applied the transformation).
6. Back in Godot, after automatic reimport finishes, drag the glb into the scene again. Somehow, the initial (unmodified) imported scene will be used instead of the newly modified glb.
7. Delete the instance you added in step 6.
8. Open the import settings by double clicking the glb file in the filesystem dock. You'll see the new (modified) scene as it should be. Click "Reimport".
9. Repeat step 6, and notice it is still using the stale (unmodified) imported scene even after manual reimport.
10. Even deleting the glb entirely, re-exporting from blender, and repeating step 6 will result in the same issue.
11. Now, *with the instance of the stale glb still open in the active scene*, repeat step 8. This time, reimport will work properly and the modified scene will appear correctly.

The only other way to make the reimport occur (if the imported scene isn't open/instanced anywhere) is to delete the .godot folder so the stale import doesn't exist anymore.

Issue is not present in 4.6.3-stable.

body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f
- Not tested in earlier versions yet

### System information

- OS: Android 15 (OPPO, model PJY110) - GPU: ARM Mali-G68 MC4 - Rendering backend: Vulkan 1.3.278 - Forward Mobile - Build fingerprint: OPPO/PJY110/OP59FB:15/AP3A.240617.008/U.24ef95f-3bc4a:user/release-keys

### Issue description

Godot crashes when the system font is changed while the app is in the background.

This happens on both the Android editor (org.godotengine.editor.v4) and an exported
game (com.mcfun.studio). It is 100% reproducible (3/3 attempts).

After changing the system font in Android Settings and switching back to Godot, the
following is observed:
1. The screen becomes slightly blurry (possibly the app being reloaded/restarted).
2. The app freezes / stutters.
3. The app force-closes, with no crash dialog.

Log evidence shows the process is killed by the system without saving state
(abnormal termination):

    am_proc_died: [0,12488,org.godotengine.editor.v4,0,2]
    wm_finish_activity: [...,proc died without state saved]

The crash buffer also contains a repeated fatal libc error at the same address,
which points to a use-after-free / access to a destroyed object related to font
cache invalidation:

    F libc : FORTIFY: pthread_mutex_lock called on a destroyed mutex (0x77fb939388)
    F libc : FORTIFY: pthread_mutex_lock called on a destroyed mutex (0x77fb939388)
    F libc : FORTIFY: pthread_mutex_lock called on a destroyed mutex (0x77fb939388)

The same mutex address (0x77fb939388) is reported every time, suggesting a
font/TextServer object that has been destroyed but is still being accessed after
the system font configuration changed.

Note: a native backtrace could not be captured because the logcat crash buffer had
already rolled over.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Godot Android editor (or an exported Godot app).
2. Send the app to the background (go to the home screen).
3. Open Android Settings and change the system font to a different one.
4. Switch back to the Godot editor / exported app.
5. The app briefly shows a blurry frame, stutters, then crashes.

body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2 and 4.8-dev6

### System information

Linux - Godot 4.7.2 - Brave browser

### Issue description

On Web, if you have looped audio playing (with the Sample playback type), pausing and unpausing the game will cause the loop to start over from the beginning.

And this won't necessarily just happen the once - in my testing, it can sometimes recur on its own, several seconds after the original pause - it'll just repeatedly start the sample over from the beginning a bunch of times, before returning to normal. But, if you don't ever pause at all, then it never happens, so it's the pause that is somehow introducing the problem.

### Steps to reproduce

I've attached an MRP below, but this is the key code:

```gdscript
func _on_button_button_up() -> void:
	%AudioStreamPlayer.playing = true
	for i in 20:
		await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout
		get_tree().paused = true
		get_tree().paused = false
		print("Toggled pause ", i + 1)
```

On a button up signal, it'll start playing a looping WAV and then every second it'll pause and unpause, which will restart the clip from the beginning.

Like I mentioned above, the issue isn't limited to just when the pause/unpause happened: it will sometimes recur many seconds later all on its own, but doing repeated pause/unpause is the fastest and most reliable way to make it happen (so you don't have to listen for like ~30 seconds to hear the restart)

title: ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_server() passes max_channels as the host's incoming bandwidth
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
- The same code is in `master` today (2026-09-29); not tested on a master build.

### System information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - headless (also seen with Forward+ on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060)

### Issue description

`ENetMultiplayerPeer::create_server()` passes `max_channels` to `ENetConnection::create_host_bound()` in the `in_bandwidth` slot, and passes `0` as `max_channels`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/modules/enet/enet_multiplayer_peer.cpp

```cpp
Error err = host->create_host_bound(bind_ip, p_port, p_max_clients, 0, p_max_channels > 0 ? p_max_channels + SYSCH_MAX : 0, p_out_bandwidth);
```

The signature is `create_host_bound(bind_address, bind_port, max_peers, max_channels, in_bandwidth, out_bandwidth)`, and `create_client()` uses it that way (`create_host_bound(bind_ip, p_local_port, 1, 0, p_in_bandwidth, p_out_bandwidth)`). So in `create_server()`:
- `max_channels = 1` makes the server announce an incoming bandwidth of 3 bytes/s (1 + `SYSCH_MAX`). ENet's bandwidth throttle on every client then lowers the packet throttle limit toward the server, so most unreliable packets from clients are dropped.
- `p_in_bandwidth` is ignored.
- The host's channel limit is always 0 (ENet's maximum), whatever `max_channels` is.

Expected: `max_channels` limits channels and `in_bandwidth` limits bandwidth, as documented.

We hit this in a voice prototype: asking for one extra channel for voice made clients drop over half of their unreliable packets, voice and movement alike. `max_channels = 0` on the server (the client still asks for its channels) avoids it.

The fix is probably to pass `p_max_channels > 0 ? p_max_channels + SYSCH_MAX : 0` as `max_channels` and `p_in_bandwidth` as `in_bandwidth`.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the script below with `godot --headless --max-fps 60 -s enet_max_channels_mrp.gd -- 1` and then `-- 0`. A client sends one small unreliable packet per frame (60 per second) to a server on localhost; the script prints the client's throttle limit toward the server and the packets the server got per second.

`max_channels = 1`:
```
create_server(24999, 32, max_channels=1)
t=1s client throttle limit=1/32, server received 54 packets
t=2s client throttle limit=32/32, server received 4 packets
t=3s client throttle limit=32/32, server received 9 packets
t=4s client throttle limit=32/32, server received 17 packets

title: Issues with symbol renaming
body:
### Tested versions

After #117949

### System information

N/A

### Issue description

Symbol renaming (#117949) was merged as an experimental feature and includes a scary confirmation dialog. That's because the feature has some known problems that need to be resolved before it can be considered fully usable.

This issue serves as a tracker for all problems affecting renaming. Report any issues here in the comments, or open a new issue and link here.

### Reliability

Symbol Rename is not much more than assisted search and replace (at least right now). It relies on code lookup to tick found occurrences, and if the lookup works incorrectly, wrong occurrences are going to be ticked.

- [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/117948
Causes false-negatives.
- [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/123918
Causes false-positives.
- [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/97988
Causes false-negatives and inability to start rename in some cases.
- [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73792
Causes false-negatives or wrong renaming.
- [ ] Lambda debug names are marked as occurences of symbols with the same name
Causes false-positives.
- [ ] Can't start renaming at an enum value declaration
Also causes false-negatives, because value declaration is not recognized as occurence.
- [ ] If there is an error in the script, lookup_code doesn't work correctly until the script is saved.
Causes false-negatives.
- [ ] lookup_code only works if the script is validated
Might be related to the above. Its easier to reproduce if `text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay` is long.
- [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94195
Causes false-negatives when using custom separators
- [ ] Global script class renaming does not work
For some reason code lookup does not properly return global classes. A hack is used to show the renaming option, but it actually does nothing.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c97e65a-b583-40ab-b8b1-87d8e93e9738

EDIT: Seems to only happen when the class is a type hint.

- [ ] Not all virtual methods are recognized

It looks like the total time of script functions is the sum of all the Self times: the time in this sum also counts the time in the _ready of a newly added node double. #### Example In the above screenshot (from the MRP linked below) the function `add_other` shows a long time. However, all this method do is add a node to the scene tree. The real time is in `busywait`, which is called in the `_ready` method of the added node. This method generates random numbers until 2 seconds have passed. The screenshot also shows the "Script Functions" time being incorrect. It is shown as 4 seconds, while the frame actually only takes 2 seconds. ### Steps to reproduce - Create a method that adds a node to the scene tree - in the _ready method of the node being added (or any method being called directly or indirectly by this _ready method) add some step that takes a long time - In the profiler, look at the frame where the first method is called ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [github.com/jmdejong/godot-profiler-self](https://github.com/jmdejong/godot-profiler-self) Press the button while the profiler is running and look in the profiler at the frame where the button is pressed. title: Calling "append_import_external_resource" in an EditorImportPlugin make reimported resources not emitting "Resource.changed"
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable, 4.8.dev6, 4.6.stable

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev6 - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (2560x1440 @ 180.06 Hz, 2560x1440 @ 144.00 Hz) - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1088) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads) - 31.84 GiB memory - WASAPI (96000 Hz, Surround 7.1)

### Issue description

When creating a Plugin, having 2 `EditorImportPlugin` (lets call them A and B), if A use `append_import_external_resource` to reimport another resource B during its own import, A `Resource.changed` signal does not get emitted in the editor (therefor, any tool script that rely on this event to update something do not get notified).

Note: After further testing, you don't event need to reimport another resource with a custom EditorImportPlugin. Reimporting the initial icon.svg react the same (calling `append_import_external_resource("res://icon.svg")`).

title: macOS: crash when a native submenu is freed from an `id_pressed` handler (`NativeMenuMacOS::_menu_close_cb` dereferences a freed RID)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]
- Not tested on `master`, but `_menu_close_cb()` is unchanged there as of 2026-09-29 (`platform/macos/native_menu_macos.mm`, last touched by 4c7aa7acb), so it is most likely reproducible too.

### System information

macOS 26.4 (25E246) - Godot v4.7.1.stable - Compatibility renderer - Apple M1 Pro

### Issue description

Clearing or rebuilding a native (global / status bar) menu from inside a **submenu item's** `id_pressed` handler crashes the engine:

```
ERROR: Attempting to use an uninitialized RID
   at: get_or_null (./core/templates/rid_owner.h:247)

================================================================
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 5
```

Cause, as far as I can tell from the source:

1. When the user clicks an item in a submenu, AppKit closes the menus and calls `menuDidClose:` → `NativeMenuMacOS::_menu_close()`, which queues `_menu_close_cb(rid)` with `call_deferred` (native_menu_macos.mm, around line 127).
2. The item's action is queued in `deferred_menu_calls` and runs later in `DisplayServerMacOS::process_events()` → `PopupMenu::activate_item()` → the user's `id_pressed` handler.
3. The handler calls `root_menu.clear()`. `PopupMenu::clear()` calls `submenu->unbind_global_menu()`, which calls `NativeMenu::free_menu()` on the submenu's RID immediately.
4. The queued `_menu_close_cb(rid)` then runs with the freed RID. `menus.get_or_null(p_rid)` returns `nullptr`, and the next line dereferences it without a check:

```cpp
void NativeMenuMacOS::_menu_close_cb(const RID &p_rid) {
	MenuData *md = menus.get_or_null(p_rid);
	if (md->close_cb.is_valid()) { // md is nullptr here
```

About the misleading error text: for a freed slot (validator `0xFFFFFFFF`), `get_or_null()` is supposed to return `nullptr` silently; the "uninitialized RID" message is only for allocated-but-uninitialized slots. But because `_menu_close_cb()` dereferences the result unconditionally, the compiler treats the `nullptr` paths as unreachable and merges them: in the official 4.7.1 macOS binary, the function that references the strings `"_menu_close_cb"` and `"Failed to execute menu close callback: %s."` branches on a validator mismatch straight into a block that prints `Attempting to use an uninitialized RID` (rid_owner.h:247) and then executes `brk #1`. The crash report's faulting address is that `brk`. So any stale RID here shows up as "uninitialized RID" + signal 5.

title: Inspector dock's "Show in FileSystem" can be invoked via its shortcut while showing as disabled, crashing with an ERR_FAIL_COND
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.8.dev (e16296832)

I have not tested other versions in this session, but this is very unlikely to be a recent regression: `InspectorDock::_get_current_resource()` (the function the crashing code path relies on) has only ever cast the currently inspected object to `Resource`, with no history of ever handling a plain `Node`, and the popup's disabled-state refresh timing described below has been the same since this dock's "resource extra" popup was introduced. I could not find any commit that changed this behavior.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (e16296832) - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (12 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The Inspector dock has a "resource extra" `MenuButton` popup (New Resource / Load Resource / Save / Save As / Edit Resource from Clipboard / Copy Resource / **Show in FileSystem** / Open Documentation / Make Resource Built-In), with several of its items also bound to a user-assignable keyboard shortcut (none of them ship with a default keybinding).

When the object currently shown in the Inspector is a **Node** rather than a **Resource** (for example, a node that is itself the root of an externally instantiated scene), the "Show in FileSystem" item is correctly shown as disabled if you actually open this popup. However, pressing its assigned shortcut *without* first opening the popup for this selection still runs the action, and it crashes with:

```
ERROR: Condition "current_res.is_null()" is true.
   at: _menu_option_confirm (editor/docks/inspector_dock.cpp:108)
```

Root cause: `MenuButton::shortcut_input()` dispatches to `PopupMenu::activate_item_by_event()`, which does correctly check `is_item_disabled()` before running the bound action -- but only against whatever disabled-state was last written to that specific item. Most of this popup's items (Save, Save As, Copy Resource, Make Resource Built-In, Open Documentation) have their disabled-state recomputed on every Inspector selection change (`InspectorDock::update()`). "Show in FileSystem" (and "Edit Resource from Clipboard") are the exception: their disabled-state is only recomputed when the popup is actually opened (`_prepare_resource_extra_popup()`, connected to the button's `about_to_popup` signal). So a pure keyboard shortcut press, without ever opening the popup for t

title: Disabled buttons report as enabled to screen readers (AT-SPI state not updated)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable, 4.5.stable (the version that introduced screen reader support). Not tested in versions in between.

### System information

Ubuntu 26.04 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Vulkan (Forward+) - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS (16 threads)

### Issue description

Disabled buttons are exposed to AT-SPI with the same state as enabled buttons. A screen reader user tabbing onto a disabled button hears it announced as a normal, usable button.

`GetState` on an enabled and a disabled button in the same scene returns the identical bitmask:

```
au 2 1124075776 0   # enabled
au 2 1124075776 0   # disabled
```

Decodes to `ENABLED | FOCUSABLE | SENSITIVE | SHOWING | VISIBLE` for both. Same result whether `disabled` is set in the scene file or at runtime via GDScript, and same result on both 4.5.stable and 4.7.2.stable.

Labels do get a different state (no `FOCUSABLE`), so the bridge isn't ignoring node state in general, it just isn't propagating `Button.disabled`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the attached project (MRP incoming as a follow-up comment).
2. Tab to "Enabled Button", then "Disabled Button" with a screen reader running.
3. Both announce the same way.

To inspect the state directly without a screen reader:

```bash
AT_SPI_ADDR=$(busctl --user call org.a11y.Bus /org/a11y/bus org.a11y.Bus GetAddress | cut -d'"' -f2)
busctl --address="$AT_SPI_ADDR" list | grep -i godot
busctl --address="$AT_SPI_ADDR" call <conn> <button-path> org.a11y.atspi.Accessible GetState
```

### Minimal reproduction project

3 files, no script, `.godot/` excluded. Attaching as a follow-up comment since `gh` can't upload zip archives directly. Scene contents:

title: Advancing animations for CollisionShapes multiple times a physics tick breaks the animation
body:
### Tested versions

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev6 - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (2880x1920 @ 119.97 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840U w/ Radeon  780M Graphics (16 threads) - 30.64 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

This is an issue from a workaround to #123861 
Because it is not reliable right now to have animation tracks default to the values of the RESET animation, we are first playing the RESET animation, mixing it and then playing the intended animation.

This works well but animating CollisionShapes multiple times in a single physics tick break the animation.
The position, shape and disabled state of the CollisionShape might ignore the animation temporarily or entirely.

In the example MRP I am playing a "left" and "right" animation that is animating the respective shapes.
I also always first play the RESET animation an use `advance(0)` to make sure it is mixed.
If I switch back and forth between the animations without letting them finish, the CollisionShapes gets animated inconsistently. You can tell by them getting offset from the similar MeshInstance3D node.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d51e328e-bded-4cc7-a2a1-bb56bdccb782

It looks like there is no way to safely animate CollisionShape properties without potentially running into this issue.
That's why we are forced to use a custom tool class that extends the AnimationPlayer. The class offers placeholder properties that are animated instead and the `mixer_applied` signal is used to apply the changes to the real CollisionShape properties once.

### Steps to reproduce

See MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

In this MRP I am brute forcing this bug to happen by doing the following steps when starting an animation:
1. Play the RESET animation
2. Use `advance(0)` to mix the animation result so it is actually resetting all the values
3. Play the intended animation
4. Again use `advance(0)` to immediately mix the result again (This seems unnecessary but makes sure that the CollisionShape properties are reliably mixed during the physics process instead of at the end of idle time)

title: Animating Shape/Mesh properties do not reliably RESET on determistic AnimtionPlayers
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducable in 4.7, 4.8 dev6

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev6 - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (2880x1920 @ 119.97 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840U w/ Radeon  780M Graphics (16 threads) - 30.64 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

For player animations in a fighting game I am primarily animating the collision shapes of Area3D nodes.
This mainly affects the properties `position`, `disabled` and `radius` / `size` of the shape.

I enabled the `deterministic` property of the AnimatonPlayer to make sure that all tracks use the RESET animation as a default value.
This works mostly well but not for any of the shape properties! 

### Steps to reproduce

Check out the MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[MRP_collisions_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32685016/MRP_collisions_bug.zip)

The above project already set up the Collision Shapes and other nodes. They are all animated to see what part of the animation works and what not. The AnimationPlayer is also set to deterministic.

(Make sure to launch the game with 'Visible Collision Shapes' enabled.

Press either left arrow key to animate the sphere or right arrow key to animate the box.
You will see that the animated shapes are raised in their position, reshaped and disabled. The other shape will be put back to the RESET values.

The issue is that the mesh and shape properties like `radius` and `size` are not set to the RESET value but instead the initial value of the previously active animation!
But if you start the same animation twice in succession, the `size` and `radius` will properly use the RESET values. 

The expected result should be that pressing left or right multiple times in succession should always show the same animation result.

title: FATAL Index p_index = -1 is out of bounds in scene cull after setting a VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES parent's visibility range to (0, 0)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (the newest release on 2026-09-26), on both Vulkan and D3D12, with the minimal project below in a fresh project folder.
- Not tested: 4.6.x and master.

### System information

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Forward+ - Vulkan 1.4.325 and D3D12 12_0 - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU (driver 592.19) - Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (Optimus laptop; NVIDIA selected with --gpu-index 0)

### Issue description

A visibility parent with `VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES` and one dependant instance crashes the engine on the next frame when the parent's visibility range is set to begin 0, end 0 (no range) while the camera stands inside the parent's begin fade band:

```text
ERROR: FATAL: Index p_index = -1 is out of bounds (count = 0).
   at: operator[] (./core/templates/paged_array.h:176)
CrashHandlerException: Program crashed with signal 4
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official (ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079)
```

The process exits with code -1073741795 (0xC000001D). It happens on every run on both drivers. Headless runs are not affected, because the dummy renderer has no scene cull.

**Expected:** clearing the parent's range makes the parent and its dependants always visible, with no crash.

**Workaround:** keep a non-zero end instead of clearing both values, for example `instance_geometry_set_visibility_range(parent, 0.0, 1.0e6, 0.0, 0.0, VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES)`. That runs clean on both drivers. Unlinking the dependants before the clear has not been tested.

**Possible cause (a hypothesis from the symptoms, not checked against the source):** with begin and end both 0 the parent leaves the scenario's visibility-range list (its visibility index becomes -1), but the "fade children" state from the previous cull stays on the parent. The dependant's fade lookup then indexes that list with -1. The count is 0 here because the parent was the only instance with a range.

1. Create a parent instance P 300 m in front of the camera, with a begin range of 300 m, a begin margin of 25 m and VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES.
2. Create a child instance C 10 m in front of the camera and call instance_set_visibility_parent(C, P).
3. Render a few frames with the camera inside P's begin fade band (275-325 m from P).
4. Call instance_geometry_set_visibility_range(P, 0, 0, 0, 0, VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES).

title: TLS fails on Windows with Avast HTTPS scanning: bundled mbedTLS rejects Avast's root certificate (empty AuthorityKeyIdentifier)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.2-stable (self-compiled with `precision=double` and .NET; `thirdparty/mbedtls` unmodified, mbedTLS 3.6.7).

### System information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Avast Antivirus with HTTPS scanning enabled (default)

### Issue description

Avast intercepts TLS and re-signs server certificates with its own root "Avast Web/Mail Shield Root", which it installs into the Windows ROOT store. Godot loads that store, but the bundled mbedTLS cannot parse this root because it has an empty AuthorityKeyIdentifier extension (`30 00`). Godot logs `Error parsing X509 certificates ... -9568` (`-0x2560`) and "1 certificates skipped", and every intercepted connection then fails with `-0x2700` (certificate verify failed). Schannel, OpenSSL and browsers accept the same root.

Effect: `WebSocketPeer` (wss) and `HTTPRequest` (https) fail with a TLS handshake error on any machine with Avast HTTPS scanning. The only workarounds are an exception in the antivirus or `TLSOptions.client_unsafe()`, neither of which is reasonable to ask of players.

Upstream bug: Mbed-TLS/mbedtls#10253 (open since 2025-06, still unfixed on `development`); a PR with a fix and tests is being prepared there. Until it lands in the 3.6 LTS branch, a small patch in `thirdparty/mbedtls/patches` would fix it: in `x509_get_authority_key_id()` (`library/x509_crt.c`), right after the `*p + len != end` check:

```c
    /* All fields are OPTIONAL, so an empty SEQUENCE is valid. */
    if (*p == end) {
        return 0;
    }
```

(Edited: an earlier version suggested treating `MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_OUT_OF_DATA` like `UNEXPECTED_TAG`. That is too loose, since `OUT_OF_DATA` is also returned for a `[0]` tag with a missing or truncated length.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows with Avast installed, HTTPS scanning on.
2. Request an HTTPS URL that Avast intercepts (github.com was intercepted here):

```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready():
	var request := HTTPRequest.new()
	add_child(request)
	request.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _headers, _body): print(result, " ", code))
	request.request("https://github.com")
```

3. Result is `RESULT_TLS_HANDSHAKE_ERROR`; the same request succeeds in a browser on that machine.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The script above on an empty scene is the whole project. The bug needs Avast's certificate in the Windows store, so it will not reproduce on machines without Avast.

title: Callable.is_valid() is unreliable for native static method Callables and breaks Callable.bind()
body:
### Tested versions

* Reproducible in: **Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]**
* Not tested: earlier stable versions
* Not tested: development snapshots

Reproduced using an official Godot build without GDExtensions, C++ modules, or editor plugins.

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.12001) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 63.90 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I found that the result returned by `Callable.is_valid()` is unreliable. A Callable that can actually be called can return `false`.

This seems to happen specifically when `Callable.get_object()` returns a `GDScriptNativeClass` and the target method is static, such as the static methods in `FileAccess`.

```gdscript
var callable: Callable = FileAccess.file_exists
```

This is a Callable that can be called successfully, but `is_valid()` returns `false`.

Then, if we bind an argument to it:

```gdscript
callable.bind("res://icon.svg")
```

the resulting Callable changes from callable to uncallable. Calling `call()` on it produces an error.

I found that the reason is that `Callable::is_valid()` uses the following code:

```cpp
return get_object() && get_object()->has_method(get_method());
```

For a `GDScriptNativeClass` object, `has_method()` returns `false` for this native static method.

However, `Callable::callp()` does not rely on `is_valid()`. Instead, it uses `ClassDB::get_method("FileAccess", "file_exists")` to find the method and execute it. This is why the original Callable can still be called successfully.

After binding arguments, the Callable changes to a custom Callable, so `bound.is_custom() == true`.

At this point, `Callable::callp()` checks `is_valid()` for the custom Callable and reports an error. As a result, the Callable with bound arguments can no longer be called.

My conclusion is that the result of `Callable.is_valid()` is not reliable. It does not accurately reflect whether a Callable can actually be called. Furthermore, this unreliable result causes a Callable that has arguments bound with `bind()` to become uncallable.

### Minimal reproduction project

A minimal reproduction project is attached to this issue.

[mbp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32754909/mbp.zip)

title: Scene properties that reference external subresources modify their paths and make the internal subresources on save.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in 4.71 and 4.8 latest

### System information

Windows 11 and Mac OS X and Kubuntu

### Issue description

When saving a scene, external subreferences are not respected as external references, but have their paths modified and are made internal. Not just duplicates, the original owning resources now point to the saved scene. 
The problem seems to be because ```ResourceFormatSaverTextInstance::_find_resources``` checks ```res->is_built_in()``` , which will always be true for subresource paths(any path with "::" is seen as built in)
The resource saver assumes the level owns this resource and modifies it's path and saves it inside the scene file.
These resources should be marked as external as they have a valid path outside the scene.

My intention was to bundle several generated textures and materials from asset imports into subresources to avoid clutter, but textures and materials need to be assigned to exported properties to render in most nodes, triggering this issue. The workaround is to not use subresources and to export each asset as it's own resource.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a custom resource with a subresource texture, generate a 1x1 ImageTexture in code. attach your custom resource to a Sprite2D property, in that node's code get the subresource and assign it to Sprite2D's texture.
The subresource will have the correct path until you save the scene.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

title: Wayland: captured mouse motion uses accelerated deltas (dx), unlike X11 and Windows which use raw input
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (`ed1daf0bf`, Arch Linux package)
- The relevant code is unchanged on `master` as of 2026-09-24

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Manjaro Linux (kernel 7.2.4) - KDE Plasma 6.7.5 (KWin 6.7.5), Wayland session - Vulkan (Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (driver 580.178.04)

### Issue description

With `Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED`, `InputEventMouseMotion.screen_relative` (and `relative`) carries **raw, unaccelerated** motion on X11 and Windows, but **compositor-accelerated** motion on Wayland. A mouse-look camera therefore turns at a different, speed-dependent rate depending only on the display driver and the user's desktop pointer-acceleration profile, and no sensitivity multiplier in the game can correct it.

Where it comes from:

- **X11**: `display_server_x11.cpp`, `XI_RawMotion` handler, reads `raw_event->raw_values` (unaccelerated).
- **Windows**: `display_server_windows.cpp`, captured mode, reads `RIM_TYPEMOUSE` raw input (`lLastX` / `lLastY`, unaccelerated).
- **Wayland**: `wayland_thread.cpp`, `_wp_relative_pointer_on_relative_motion`, stores `dx` / `dy` (accelerated) in `pd.relative_motion`. `dx_unaccel` / `dy_unaccel` are received and ignored. `pd.relative_motion * scale` then becomes the event's `relative` and `screen_relative`.

`zwp_relative_pointer_v1` sends both values precisely so that clients such as games can have motion "without pointer acceleration applied".

**Measured.** I read the mouse's own evdev `REL_X`/`REL_Y` counts (`/dev/input/event*`) at the same time as the project below logged `screen_relative`, aligned the two streams by timestamp, and computed gain = Godot px / raw counts in 50 ms windows, grouped by how fast the mouse was moving. Mouse on KDE's default **Adaptive** acceleration profile, speed 0:

| mouse speed (raw counts/s) | X11 gain, median | Wayland gain, median (run 2) | Wayland (run 1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–1,000 | 1.00 | 1.10 | 1.22 |
| 1,000–3,000 | 1.04 | 2.02 | 1.98 |
| 3,000–8,000 | 1.02 | 2.01 | 2.05 |
| 8,000–20,000 | 1.03 | 2.08 | (not reached) |
| > 20,000 | 1.05 | 2.13 | (not reached) |

X11 is flat at every speed, as raw input should be: one run, about 1.29 M raw counts, stream correlation 0.81. Wayland follows the desktop's acceleration curve: about 1× for slow motion and about 2× for anything faster, and the two Wayland runs agree (run 2: about 1.31 M raw counts, correlation 0.81). Measured on one mouse and one desktop. Separately, s
[truncated]

title: [Web] Audio sample playback ignores pitch_scale for autoplay, and 2nd+ loops.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2 (and latest master ca871ccc9cd8e5c2ce829ec5c0fae1ac32c6269f). it's likely reproducible since the beginning of web samples playback, but at least as far back as [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93362/changes#diff-9008639a3ed62166e1681f16d4c2149f83209ff5327f500dd795843a1747076aR638)

### System information

Intel MBP 15.7.9 - AMD Radeon Pro 5300M 4 GB Intel UHD Graphics 630 - but shouldn't matter.

### Issue description

I know the guidance in the issue template says to submit separate issues for separate bugs, but these two bugs can be fixed by the same LOC change, and are closely related to one another (just with a slight twist).

I have put together a small fix for this and will open a PR shortly. 

For web samples playback, pitch_scale is ignored in two cases: 
1. AudioStreamPlayer with autoplay=true (works fine when calling .play() directly)
2. On the 2nd+ loops of a sample

The autoplay flavor of this bug has an additional codepath that seems to be broken (or at least, unintentionally called): the `pause(enable:bool)` method calls `_unpause`, which then unconditionally calls `_restart`, regardless of if the stream was playing or not. 

(no ai used at all.)

### Steps to reproduce

Autoplay bug:
1. Add AudioStreamPlayer to scene
2. Set autoplay=true
4. Set pitch_scale=2
5. Run scene: audio is playing at pitch_scale=1.

Loop bug:
1. Add AudioStreamPlayer to scene
2. Set autoplay=false
3. Set pitch_scale=2
4. Add an audio stream that has looping enabled
5. Attach script, `_ready(): player.play()` (important!)
6. Run scene: audio will play with pitch_scale=2 properly, until it loops. at this point, pitch_scale is 1.0.

The cause of the pitch_scale problems is that _restart does not sync the playback rate when it creates a new AudioBufferSourceNode. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This scene is configured to test both of these bugs. 

[pitch_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32592806/pitch_mrp.zip)

title: load_threaded_request -  issues with relative paths that point to the same resource
body:
### Tested versions

Cusotm-Build based on tagged branch "[4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/tag/4.7.2-stable)"

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.rc (7160efa07) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX 3500 Ada Generation Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9671) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13950HX (32 threads) - 63.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The issue is related to calling `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` using relative paths that point to the same resource. 

Example Situation: 
- Real Path: res://Art/Explosion_01.png
- Relative Path A: res:://Actor/BigExplosion/../../Art/Explosion_01.png
- Relative Path B: res:://Actor/Ninja/Disappear/../../../Art/Explosion_01.png

If I typed them correct, both relative paths point to the same `Explosion_01.png` resource. 

You can call into `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with both relative paths, and the system returns an `Error::OK` for both calls. Calls into `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get_status` also properly track the "load" progress of both relative paths. 

However, calling `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` on both relative paths can cause issues.

When building Godot i ndebug mode, the above can reliably cause a `DEV_ASSERT` to be hit at line 950 of `resource_loader.cpp` (inside `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get`)

When running the Godot editor in release mode, this can "sometimes" result in the 2nd call to `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` to return a null resource instead of the successfully loaded resource. 

#### Our Investigation: 
From our own investigation, inside `ResourceLoader::_load_start`, the 2 different relative paths are both being given their own `LoadToken` with `LoadToken::user_rc = 1`. 

Then, when the loading is complete and ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get is called twice, but upon the second call, the `LoadToken::user_rc == 0`, hitting the dev assert and, likely, causing the return resource to be null sometimes.

#### Our Workaround
We have found that resolving relative paths before we call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` (using `String::simplify_path`) prevents the issue.

1. Have a resource in the project folder
2. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with a relative path to the resource (`RelPathA`)
3. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with a "different" relative path to the resource (`

title: Release export: "Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection ... Signal: 'tree_exited'" when resetting a SceneMultiplayer peer after an RPC
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible (release export template only): v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]
- Not reproducible with the same project: editor binary, and the v4.7.2 **debug** export template

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64), headless (`--headless`), Linux export templates from the official 4.7.2 / 4.7 downloads

### Issue description

Replacing the `multiplayer_peer` of a `SceneMultiplayer` after at least one RPC has been sent through it prints, in a **release** export only:

```
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from 'Endpoint:<Node#25350374771>'. Signal: 'tree_exited', callable: ''.
```

`SceneCacheInterface` connects each cached node with a **bound** callable and `CONNECT_ONE_SHOT`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf/modules/multiplayer/scene_cache_interface.cpp#L46

but `SceneCacheInterface::clear()` disconnects the **unbound** form:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf/modules/multiplayer/scene_cache_interface.cpp#L301

The same two lines are unchanged on `master`. The debug template disconnects cleanly; the release template reports the connection as nonexistent, so matching the unbound callable against the bound connection appears to behave differently between build types. This looks related to #95512 (release-only `tree_exiting` disconnect error, GCC LTO) and to #119740 / #120394, but #120394 is already in 4.7.1+ and this still reproduces on 4.7.2.

Workaround (verified with the MRP below, release template, 3/3 clean runs): free every node that was used for an RPC before changing or clearing the peer, so its one-shot `tree_exited` callback removes the cache entry first. Adding `endpoint.free()` before the peer reset removes the error.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the three files below in an empty project with `run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"` (a `main.tscn` with a single `Node` root using `main.gd`).
2. Export with the Linux preset using the **release** template (`--export-release`).
3. Run the exported binary with `--headless`. It prints `REPRO RPC DELIVERED`, `REPRO RESET LIVE API` and the error above, then exits.
4. Run the same project from the editor binary, or a debug export: no error.

title: LightmapGI dilation overwrites texels that already contain valid baked lighting
LightmapGI bakes incorrect indirect light inside opaque double-sided geometry
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
- 4.8.dev, master 39216f0c8
- 4.7.2.stable

Historical comparison:
- 4.3.stable does not show the same behavior in an equivalent synthetic scene (not the MRP, see "Additional information").

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (RKL GT1) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-11400 @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 31.14 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

The issue was also reproduced on master 39216f0c8 on Windows 11.

### Issue description

LightmapGI bakes indirect environment light into geometry that is fully enclosed inside an opaque double-sided volume.

The MRP contains two identical closed opaque boxes, each with a smaller cube inside:

- one box uses `CULL_DISABLED`;
- the other uses the default `CULL_BACK` as a control.

There are no lights in the scene. The only illumination is the LightmapGI environment, using a white custom color.

The outer boxes are hidden from the camera for clarity, but they still participate in the LightmapGI bake.

The denoiser is disabled.

After baking on master 39216f0c8, the cube inside the `CULL_DISABLED` box is clearly illuminated, while the equivalent `CULL_BACK` control remains almost black.

The enclosed cube has no visibility to the environment, so this lighting is invalid.

The cause appears to be in `trace_ray()` in `modules/lightmapper_rd/lm_compute.glsl`.

`trace_ray()` applies the material cull mode before returning whether the hit was on the geometric front or back.

For `CULL_DISABLED` materials, a geometric back-face hit is therefore reported as `RAY_FRONT` and the geometric side of the hit is lost.

During baking this causes two problems:

- the unocclude pass checks for `RAY_BACK` to detect texels located inside geometry; with `CULL_DISABLED` it never sees a geometric back face;
- indirect bounce rays that hit the inside of opaque double-sided geometry are shaded as front-face hits, using the outward-facing side of the triangle, so the bounce can leave the volume and collect environment light that the enclosed texel cannot see.

The per-triangle cull mode was added to the lightmapper in #99538 together with transparency support.

The transparency support itself is not the problem.

The issue is that geometric hit side and material cull behavior are combined too early in `trace_ray()`.

title: launching the engine with --embedded outside the editor crashes immediately on MacOS
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.7.2.stable.official (ed1daf0bf), official macOS build
Also present on current master (0f1b62b7) — same code

### System information

macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro 

### Issue description

On macOS, launching the engine with --embedded outside the editor crashes immediately with signal 11, before anything is rendered. It happens with the default Metal driver and with --rendering-driver opengl3, in a brand new empty project.

The backtrace points repeatedly at mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert (MoltenVK), which is misleading — the crash happens before any shader work; the symbolizer appears to be resolving to the nearest exported symbol.

The cause looks like a null dereference: the DisplayServerMacOSEmbedded constructor in platform/macos/display_server_macos_embedded.mm calls EngineDebugger::get_singleton()->send_message("game_view:set_context_id", ...), and that singleton only exists when the editor launched the process. There are six more unguarded send_message calls in the same file (mouse mode, warp mouse, IME, cursor). OS_MacOS_Embedded::alert() in platform/macos/os_macos.mm already null-checks before the same kind of call.

Crash:
```
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official (ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079)
[1] libsystem_platform.dylib - _sigtramp + 56
[2] mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert(...)
[3] mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert(...)
````

### Steps to reproduce

- On macOS, create a new empty project (one empty scene set as the main scene is enough). Nothing else in it.
- Quit the editor. The project must not be running from it - the crash is about running without the editor attached.
- From a terminal, run the official Godot binary directly on that project with the --embedded flag:
/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --embedded --path /path/to/project --quit-after 120

Expected: the project runs with no window of its own, as it does when the editor embeds it.
Actual: it crashes immediately with Program crashed with signal 11, before anything renders. Exit code 134.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

title: Microsoft Japanese IME overwrites the last converted segment when typing without explicitly confirming the conversion
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2 stable (`ed1daf0bf`)
- Not reproduced when Windows is configured to use the previous version of Microsoft IME
- Earlier Godot versions have not been tested

### System information

Windows 11 Home, build 26200 - Godot 4.7.2 stable - Compatibility renderer (OpenGL 3.3) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, driver 32.0.16.1692

### Issue description

When using the current Microsoft Japanese IME in a `LineEdit` or `TextEdit`, typing a new character immediately after converting Japanese text, without pressing Enter to explicitly confirm the conversion, replaces the last converted segment.

For example:

1. Type `yamakawa`.
2. Press Space to convert it to `山川`.
3. Without pressing Enter, type `a`.

Expected display:

```text
山川あ
```

```text
山あ
```

The last converted segment, `川`, is replaced by the new composition text. This occurs in both LineEdit and TextEdit.

The issue does not occur when either of the following workarounds is used:
- Press Enter to explicitly confirm `山川` before typing `a`.
- Enable “Use previous version of Microsoft IME” in the Windows Microsoft IME compatibility settings.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11, enable the current Microsoft Japanese IME.
2. Create a project containing either a LineEdit or a TextEdit.
3. Run the project and focus the text control.
4. Enable Hiragana input.
5. Type `yamakawa`.
6. Press Space to convert the text to `山川`.
7. Do not press Enter.
8. Type `a`.
9. Observe that the field displays `山あ` instead of `山川あ`. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A project containing only a focused LineEdit is sufficient to reproduce the issue. The issue is also reproducible after replacing the LineEdit with a TextEdit.

title: String.to_float() counts leading zeros against its 18-digit limit: "00000000000000000001.5" parses as 0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (4.7.2.stable.arch_linux.ed1daf0bf)
- Not a regression: the same `built_in_strtod()` digit-counting code (`if (mantSize > 18)`) is present in the 1.0-stable, 3.6-stable, 4.0-stable and 4.6-stable sources and is unchanged on master, so the bug has likely existed since Godot 1.0.

### System information

Linux - Arch - Godot 4.7.2 stable

### Issue description

Tested versions: Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable. The parser is unchanged on master.

System information: Godot v4.7.2.stable.arch_linux (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux - Linux 7.2.6-arch2-1 (x86_64). This is core string parsing, so it doesn't depend on the platform.

Issue description:
`String.to_float()` reads at most 18 digit characters, and leading zeros count toward that limit. The same parser is used by `float(String)`, `str_to_var()`, `JSON.parse_string()` and GDScript float literals. Fixed-point numbers with many leading zeros get truncated or read as 0, even though they pass `is_valid_float()`:

| input | result | expected |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `"00000000000000000001.5"` | `0` | `1.5` |
| `"0.0000000000000000271"` | `2e-17` | `2.71e-17` |
| `"271e-19"` | `2.71e-17` | `2.71e-17` |

**Cause:** [`built_in_strtod()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/core/string/ustring.cpp#L2445-L2505) counts every digit, leading zeros included, caps the count at 18, and reads the first 18 digits. Significant digits past that point are dropped. Skipping leading zeros before counting would fix it.

**Related, lower priority:** the parser is also not correctly rounded. About 1 in 6 of the shortest decimals printed by `String.num_scientific()` read back 1 ulp off, so `float(String.num_scientific(v)) == v` fails for some `v`. For example, `"1.8143934130161599"` reads as `1.81439341301616`. `"1e-320"` reads as `0` because 10^320 overflows before the divide. A correctly rounded, locale-independent parser such as [fast_float](https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float) would fix both.

Steps to reproduce: godot --headless --script repro.gd
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _init() -> void:
      for s in ["00000000000000000001.5", "0.0000000000000000271", "271e-19", "1.8143934130161599", "1e-320"]:
              print("%-24s -> %s" % [s, String.num_scientific(float(s))])
      quit()
```
Steps to reproduce: godot --headless --script repro.gd
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _init() -> void:
      for s in ["00000000000000000001.5", "0.00000000000000

### Tested versions

- Godot v4.6.2 (Jolt Physics)

### System information

Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR)

### Issue description

If you make a `SoftBody3D` and the following conditions are met:

- The `SoftBody3D` has a `pressure_coefficient` greater than 0
- The `SoftBody3D`'s `process_mode` is toggled between `Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED` and `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`

...then it will grow in size permanently every time the `process_mode` is toggled, with seemingly no way to reset it to its original size.

In other words, it keeps expanding:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08523650-d55f-4a22-ae42-3e1a820f018d

As you can see, it keeps getting bigger. I would expect the soft body to stay the same size.

Potentially related issues:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56142 (but that was back in 2021, before Jolt Physics was integrated)
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3535

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce it, you can just run the reproduction project included below. It will automatically start toggling the `process_mode` and you should see the `SoftBody3D` expanding.

(Note: in Godot 4.6.x and below, you need to set the `SoftBody3D`'s mass to 0kg and set the pressure to about ~4000, else it will explode. [This is because the weight calculation changed between those two versions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116041). The expanding bug is still present in both versions though.)

### Tested versions

- Reproducable in v4.7.2 (macos, but general issue reported by users on linux+windows)
- *Not* reproducable in v4.6.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M1 Max - Apple M1 Max (10 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory (also reported on windows+linux)

### Issue description

REPRO SYSTEM: 
OS: MacOS M1 Tahoe V26.6.2 (25G83)
Godot v4.7.2

I was getting back some reports of my game (along with steam) stalling with low cpu usage and music still playing.  Their log files tended to end with

```
ERROR: Condition "p_elem->_root" is true.
   at: add (./core/templates/self_list.h:46)
```

Looking into it more, I assembled a test case here that reproduces a hang https://github.com/increpare/torque_callback_repro

the core of the problem for me seems to be calling apply_torque in _integrate_forces.  calling state.apply_torque works fine.

```
	func _integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState3D) -> void:
		calls += 1
		if DIRECT_STATE:
			state.apply_torque(Vector3(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)) # safe
		else:
			apply_torque(Vector3(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)) # risk of stalling
```

here are some stats on how long it took to get to a stall in each test:

```
# v4.7.2 DIRECT_STATE=false, multithreaded physics=true:
# run 1: frame ~14300
# run 2: frame ~4500
# run 3: frame ~100

# v4.7.2 DIRECT_STATE=true, multithreaded physics=false
# run 1: reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
# run 2:  reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
# run 3: reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall

# v4.7.2  direct_state=false, multithreaded physics=false
#1 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
#2 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
#3 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall

# 4.6.stable  DIRECT_STATE false, multithreaded true
#1 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
#2 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
#3 reached FRAME_LIMIT without stall
```

As you can see, it seems specific to 4.7, and specific to multithreaded being set to true.

this is possibly related to #120941

### Steps to reproduce

Load the project and hit play in godot - it should reliably hang before it hits the limit.  If you go to the settings menu and disable multithreaded physics, it should run to the end.  OR if you set DIRECT_STATE to be true in main.gd.

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Editor CPU usage increases significantly and stays elevated when the project contains a large number of small SVG files. The increase happens without opening any scene, without touching the editor, and without any additional plugin enabled.

### Steps to reproduce

**Steps** 
- Create a new empty project.
- Create a folder and copy ~600 small SVG files into it (icons of a few KB each will do).
- Open the editor and wait for the initial import to finish.
- Observe CPU usage while idle (no scenes open, no interaction, editor focused).

**Expected result:**
The editor should stay at low CPU usage (~0-1%) when idle.

**Actual result:**
CPU usage rises ~7% and stays constant even without interaction. Deleting some SVG files reduces usage proportionally; deleting all of them brings it back to normal.

title: Android: 3D Scaling decreases but never increases performance unless 0.1
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable but also many older version e.g. 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6
Platform/Hardware: Android, Samsung Galaxy A35 - ARM Mali G68 MP5

### System information

Android 16 - Godot 4.7.2.stable - ARM Mali G68 MP5 (Host: Windows 11)

### Issue description

### The Problem/Bug
Imagine a scene which, from my experience, should mostly be influenced by bandwidth/fragment shader performance. For example: 
- Renderer: Mobile (Vulkan)
- A PBR shaded full screen covering, flat ground with some cubes on it.  
- There is one Dir-Light with Ortho-Shadows and 1024 shadowmap size, quality is "hard".
- One point light in the middle of the scene, no shadows.
- Sky is disabled, no environment or other effects.
- There is one Label control showing the FPS
- The viewport size is native(2340x1080 in this case) and the render/3d scale is 1.0.
- MSAA is off as well as roughness limiter or any other things.
- Phone is mid-range Samsung Galaxy A35(2024) with ARM Mali-G68 MP5.

In Godot I get around 80-90 FPS (Mobile Renderer).
In Unity I get around 80-90 FPS (Vulkan Renderer)

So far so good. Now I enable a slightly more expensive postprocessing effect, lets say DOF Bokeh with only Near enabled.

In Godot 55 FPS
In Unity 55 FPS (70-75 with Gaussian but thats unfair)

So far so good. But now it comes:

In Unity with Render Scale 0.7: Boosts back to 120 FPS (UI at native res.)

In Godot with 3D Scaling to 0.7: Decreases FPS to 48-50. Going further down changes not much except that frame jumps get bigger(48-68 FPS) until I go to 0.1 where it increases to 85 FPS (With Compatibility-Renderer btw. I get 120 FPS as it should be).

This is not what I would expect, it makes 3D Scale pointless. It sounds like a bug to me. A more serious one tbh as some low/mid-range phones have high resolutions not really made for 3D realtime rendering I would say. 

### Further Investigations
I realized this maybe has something to do with the UI/Viewport. If I turn 3D Scale back to 1.0 and instead set the viewport size to something low like 960x540 and then stretch mode to "viewport". Then FPS in Godot boosts back to 120 FPS. And that is the part which sounds wrong to me as the only difference from before now is that in addition to the 3D scene, the UI is also scaled which is not ideal but interesting how it affects performance. In Unity is doesn't matter.

So the question is, why is having UI rendered at native resolution in Godot slows down performance so much but not in

title: Editor throws error when duplicating nested instances of scenes
body:
### Tested versions

- Regression - this was introduced by PR #120354, merged yesterday.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (57277407e) - macOS Sequoia (15.7.4) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz, 1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 (Apple9) - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

This PR #120354 accidentally introduced a bug where the editor will throw errors when duplicating nested instantiated scenes. The errors derive from `Node::_duplicate_script()` and `Node::_duplicate_properties`.

This means that properties and scripts will not be recursively duplicated for nested instances, though they should be.

This is easily fixable and I'm opening a PR shortly to fix this!

### Steps to reproduce

1) In a brand new project, create two scenes (main.tscn and subscene.tscn).
2) Add a root node to main.tscn and save it.
2) Add a root node AND a single child node subscene.tscn and save subscene.tscn.
3) Add an instance of subscene.tscn in the main scene, and save main.tscn.
4) Right click on the root node of main.tscn, click Copy, and observe the errors:
```
- ERROR: Node not found: "Subscene/SubsceneChild" (relative to "Subscene").
- ERROR: Child node disappeared while duplicating.
- ERROR: Node not found: "Subscene/SubsceneChild" (relative to "Subscene").
- ERROR: Child node disappeared while duplicating.
```

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 14 Sep 2026 22:41:30 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 615.71.09) - AMD Ryzen 5 2600 Six-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

If you set `display/window/size/window_width_override` and `display/window/size/window_height_override` values and start the game, the window is indeed set to this overridden size.

But if you start the game in `FULLSCREEN` and then go out of `FULLSCREEN into `WINDOWED` the screen height is smaller.

This is how I handle toggling fullscreen:
```
func toggle_fullscreen() -> void:
	if window_mode == DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
		window_mode = DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED
	elif window_mode != DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
		window_mode = DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN
	
	DisplayServer.window_set_mode(window_mode)

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventKey:
		var key: InputEventKey = event as InputEventKey
		if key.keycode == KEY_F11 && !key.pressed:
			toggle_fullscreen()
```

Maybe this is an incorrect way to do this and that's why it happens?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffde7050-761f-4a98-8e8c-051cf2eaefcf

On a related note: I also found that I can't set the window's height to more than 1040px (I have a 1080p monitor). I'm quite certain that 40px is the taskbar height. I'm not sure if Godot doesn't not let me do that or it's the OS itself (so you don't hide the taskbar).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project.
2. Add code above to a script.
3. Set window size overrides.
4. Set window to start WINDOWED and run the game. Check window height against the 2D ruler (on 100% zoom i.e. 1:1)
5. Set window to start WINDOWED and run the game. Check window height against the 2D ruler and see that the window's height is smaller.

Follow-up to #123468 which I closed.

After I migrated [my project](https://github.com/MewPurPur/GodSVG) to Godot 4.6.1, I suddenly noticed a very sharp increase in executable size. I've only reproduced this on my project with 4.6 vs 4.6.1 web exports and quite specific buildsystem options, but ZIPs for other versions and platforms have also bloated up way more than expected, so they might have this problem too.

title: Compute Shader Indirect Dispatch Buffer Visibility Issue
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on v4.8.dev5.mono.official [9552dfb68]
Also tested it on 4.5, and the exact same behavior is observed.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev5.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 7 1700 Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.95 GiB memory - WASAPI (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

(If I am providing too little information, let me know and I will try to flesh it out in the ways you want)

I run a compute list on the default rendering device with the following compute shaders:
1. Prepare an indirect arg buffer with a direct dispatch. Workgroups: (x=1, y=1, z=1)
2. Dispatch several indirect dispatches all using the same indirect arg buffer for their workgroups
3. Observe that depending on what the indirect dispatches do, and which buffers are bound to them, not all of them will see the changes written to the indirect arg buffer in step 1.

### Steps to reproduce

### Setup
3 shaders:
prepare_indirect: Write indirect buffer
add_to_buffer: Use indirect buffer 1
write_to_buffer: Use indirect buffer 2

(The actions performed add/write are not important, and are just used to showcase the issue. It is the binding and writing itself that seems to be of consequence.)

4 buffers:
args: indirect args
countA: a counter to increment
countB: another counter to increment
other: something else to bind and write to

### The following sequence (not exclusively) is an example that seem to trigger the issue: *(dispatch_0 in MRP)*
1. Direct dispatch (workgroups: 1,1,1): Bind and write to args (shader: prepare_indirect)
2. Indirect dispatch (workgroups: args): Bind and add to countA (shader: add_to_buffer)
3. Indirect dispatch (workgroups: args): Bind and write to other (shader: write_to_buffer)
4. Indirect dispatch (workgroups: args): Bind and add to countB (shader: add_to_buffer)

title: `NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED` duplicate name with different node name casing than default
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf

### System information

Linux Mint 22.3 Zena

### Issue description

When using `camelCase`, `snake_case` or `kebab-case` options for `editor/naming/node_name_casing` project setting, and I add two nodes of same custom script class, the `NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED` notification fires two times on editor, the first one when the node is created and the second one when the name changes according to the project setting and (**should**) validate duplicate names, adding a number suffix.

When using the default value `PascalCase` (maybe should be renamed to `unchanged`, more on that later) and adding two nodes via the global script class name `Test`, I have the following output:

```
[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'Test'
'Test' entered tree

[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'Test2'
'Test2' entered tree
```

As expected, the second node receives the second new name with the correct suffix. But when using other name casing options, for example `snake_case`, it gives the following output:
```
[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'test'
'test' entered tree

[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'test'
'test2' entered tree
```

Notice how the number suffix is only added *after* the node is already added to the tree, and the second new name doesn't have the suffix.

Also, about the `PascalCase` default option for the project setting, it doesn't actually enforce the casing. For example, if by class is named `test`, I would expect the default option rename it to `Test`, but this isn't what happens, it simply leaves the name casing untouched. The output for the default option is:

```

[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'test'

'test' entered tree

[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'test' renamed to 'test2'
