title: GraphEdit zoom/pan is O(n^2) in node count. causing laggy/stuttery zoom feel
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.7.1-stable

### System information

Windows 10, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070, Compatibility (OpenGL 3.3) renderer.

### Issue description

Symptom: When using a large number of nodes in GraphEdit, for example 600, scroll-wheel zooming becomes extremely laggy, at roughly 280 ms per frame.
Expected: Smooth zooming.
Additional information: Based on inference, the call chain behavior in `scene/gui/graph_edit.cpp` is as follows:
1. During zoom/pan, `_update_scroll_offset()` is deferred, and it iterates over all GraphElement child nodes, calling `set_position()` and `set_scale()` on each node.
2. Each `set_scale()` synchronously triggers that node's `item_rect_changed` signal.
3. That signal is connected to `_graph_node_rect_changed()`, which unconditionally executes `callable_mp(...).call_deferred(_update_top_connection_layer)` for every node.
4. The first line of each deferred callback in turn calls `_update_scrollbars()`, which again iterates over all nodes to compute the canvas bounding box.
Therefore, n nodes produce n deferred callbacks, and each callback performs another O(n) full traversal, resulting in an overall complexity of O(n²).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached Minimal Reproduction Project (MRP) and run the game directly.
2. On the GraphEdit canvas in the running game, scroll the mouse wheel directly.
3. Observe the obvious lag on each zoom.

title: FontVariation.variation_opentype ignores documented String axis aliases such as "wght"
body:
### Tested Version

master dfa06cafb4

### System Information

Windows 10 Pro, headless, Advanced text server

### Issue Description

The key for the `FontVariation.variation_opentype` dictionary specifies an axis. According to the documentation, the axis can be specified by either a numeric tag or a name (String); it notes that some axes may have multiple names—for instance, `wght` and `weight` refer to the same axis. In reality, however, `weight` works, whereas `wght` does not and is ignored. No error is thrown, and the font remains at its default weight; in short, the key specified in the documentation does not work.

I tested this using the same font, text, and size; the only variable was whether I wrote `weight` or `wght`:
                          wght=100  wght=900
int (tag)  :            117 px         140 px
"weight" :            117 px         140 px
"wght"    :           '130 px'        '130 px'
(no coordinates) :130 px        130 px

The same error exists in three files: the code checks only the numeric tag and the name returned by `tag_to_name()`, without passing String keys through `name_to_tag()`.

Files:
`scene/resources/font.cpp` lines 2419 and 2423
`modules/text_server_adv/text_server_adv.cpp` line 2139
`modules/text_server_fb/text_server_fb.cpp` line 1038

There is an additional consequence: since an unrecognized key is treated as the default in both cases, different values ​​collapse onto the same font RID (the cache returns the same entry).

`editor/themes/editor_fonts.cpp:292` -> uses the "weight" string directly.
`editor/gui/code_editor.cpp:1723` -> converts user input via `name_to_tag()` first.

In other words, advising users to use only the tag is inconsistent with the engine's own code.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project in Godot once so the font gets imported
2. Run the scene
3. Compare the four printed values

Notes:
This is not a regression; I observed the same issues with 4.6-stable and 4.7-stable as well, though I didn't test them—I only reviewed the code.
I simply examined the code path followed by the importer; I did not compare the on-screen output.

title: [Android] Headless export fails with a completely blank configuration error when ETC2/ASTC compression is disabled
body:
**Godot version:**
4.3.stable.official

**OS/device including version:**
Ubuntu 22.04 (GitHub Actions / Headless CLI)

**Issue description:**
When attempting to export an Android project headlessly via the CLI (\godot --headless --export-release "Android"\), if ETC2/ASTC texture compression is disabled in \project.godot\, the export fails. 

However, instead of warning the user about the missing texture compression, the engine outputs a completely blank configuration error:
\\\	ext
ERROR: Cannot export project with preset "Android" due to configuration errors:

   at: _fs_changed (editor/editor_node.cpp:1012)
\\\
This makes it virtually impossible to debug headless CI pipeline failures without reading the Godot source code. (Note: The Godot Editor GUI catches this via a separate UI warning, so this bug primarily impacts headless/CLI users).

**Cause:**
In \platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp\, within the \EditorExportPlatformAndroid::has_valid_project_configuration(...)\ function, the code correctly sets \alid = false\ when ETC2/ASTC compression is missing, but **fails to append any text to the \err\ string**. 

\\\cpp
	if (!ResourceImporterTextureSettings::should_import_etc2_astc()) {
		valid = false;
        // BUG: Missing error message! e.g., err += TTR("ETC2/ASTC texture compression is required for Android.") + "\n";
	}
\\\

Because \err\ is empty, Godot prints the configuration error header, followed by a blank string.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a new Godot 4.3 project and configure an Android export preset.
2. Ensure \endering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true\ is **missing** or set to \ alse\ in \project.godot\.
3. Run the export headlessly: \godot --headless --export-release "Android" out.aab\
4. Observe the blank error output.

title: TileSet.create_tile() sorting after each tile causes compounding lag as TileSet grows
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf
- Present in source from at least 4.4-stable through 4.7-stable

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Intel Core i9-14900KF (32 threads), 62 GB RAM - Godot 4.7.2.stable, GL Compatibility, headless

### Issue description

**Note:** Cleaned up, hand written, non-AI version of #123445 as per rules.

**The Issue**

Large tileset images with many tiles lag both the game and editor when they're created and loaded. This appears to be caused by a sorting function that causes more lag the more tiles are added as it's performed after each individual tile is added to the map.

**How it was discovered**

I was testing a number of premade tilesets I'd bought off itch.io and one of them (Modern Exteriors) had an all-in-one tileset image that had everything in it (about 56K tiles). When adding the image I was prompted if I wanted all non transparent tiles set up, I hit yes and the editor lagged heavily for several minutes before completing the task, however while the tileset was visible the editor was extremely slow to the point of almost being unusable. Having it in "TileMap" mode when placing tiles, the lag didn't exist.

I found after adding some tiles to a board and booting up the game moving from one board that had a small tileset to the big one, caused minutes of load were the game would just lock up. My machine is a fair monster and can run ray-traced nonsense so I was surprised that a 7MB 2D tileset image was causing this much strain.

I wasn't sure what to do with this as whilst it was a big tileset, I refused to believe it was beyond what games were capable of, again a 7mb image is teenie tiny and ~56K rows isn't catastrophic in the grand scheme of things.

I tested having the same 56k tiles split up into separate smaller tilesets, but still all included in the same board, vastly increased load time, which was odd.

| Sources | Tiles each | Load | Speedup |
|--------:|-----------:|------:|--------:|
| 1 | 56,639 | 41.51 s | — |
| 2 | 28,320 | 20.41 s | 2.03× |
| 4 | 14,160 | 10.03 s | 4.14× |
| 8 | 7,080 | 4.99 s | 8.32× |
| 16 | 3,540 | 2.54 s | 16.33× |
| 32 | 1,770 | 1.34 s | 31.06× |

**The Cause**

With some help from that which will not be named, the problem was traced to `scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp:5014`

```
// Create and resize the tile.
tiles.insert(p_atlas_coords, tad);
tiles_ids.push_back(p_atlas_coords);

title: 3D viewport material drop tooltip shows "Hold Command" on macOS, but should say "Hold Control"
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2.stable.official (`ed1daf0bf`).
- Also observed in Godot 4.7.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (12 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When dragging a texture or material from the FileSystem dock onto a `MeshInstance3D` in the 3D viewport, the hover tooltip on macOS says to "Hold Command" to apply it as a surface material override. In reality the Control key on MacOS triggers material slot override, not the Command key.

Screenshot:
https://www.pasteboard.co/4pRumPdjPh9_.png

In my testing:

- A normal drop assigns the material to `GeometryInstance3D > Geometry > Material Override`.
- Holding Cmd produces the same whole-object material override.
- Holding the Control key instead assigns it to `MeshInstance3D > Surface Material Override`.

The tooltip and recognized modifier should agree. Either the tooltip should identify Control, or Cmd should activate the surface-override behavior.

The behavior appears consistent with `_apply_preview_material()` checking `Key::CTRL`, while the tooltip formats the modifier using `CMD_OR_CTRL`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a blank Godot project with no editor plugins, GDExtensions, or custom engine modules.
2. Create a 3D scene.
3. Add a `MeshInstance3D`.
4. Assign it a built-in `BoxMesh`.
5. Drag `icon.svg`, a texture, or a saved material from the FileSystem dock over the box.
6. Observe that the viewport tooltip says to hold Cmd for a surface material override.
7. Hold Cmd and drop the resource.
8. Select the `MeshInstance3D` and observe that `GeometryInstance3D > Geometry > Material Override` was assigned.
9. Undo or clear that override.
10. Repeat the drop while holding the physical Control key.
11. Observe that `MeshInstance3D > Surface Material Override > 0` was assigned instead.

Note that a  BoxMesh has only one mesh surface, so both results look identical on all six sides. The difference is visible in the Inspector properties described above. A mesh with multiple surfaces can also be used to make the difference visually apparent.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A newly created blank project is sufficient. No scripts or third-party plugins are required.

### Issue description

Description:
The MRP is a small AR Marker Tracking App (QR Codes).

What doesn't work:
When installing the MRP for the first time on the Quest 3, OpenXR fails to create a spatial context due to a permissions race condition. ```

Even after the permission is accepted, the built-in marker tracking does not register visible markers during that first session. When starting the app for a second time (or deploying a new build with existing permissions), the built-in marker tracking works as intended and gray spheres appear over the QR Codes.

Expected behavior:
OpenXR should either wait for the user to resolve the permission prompt before attempting to create the spatial context, or it should gracefully recover and begin tracking markers once the permission is granted during the initial session.

#### Setup MRP

### Issue description

Hey 👋 
My Claude Fable agent foudn and reported this issue while working on a project.

🤖 :

One hardware Back press delivers `NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST` twice to the same node, a few milliseconds apart. From the attached MRP — one Control, one _notification, one adb shell input keyevent 4 — on both versions:

> 4.7.2.stable   GO_BACK #1 at 4079 ms     GO_BACK #2 at 4094 ms     (15 ms)
> 4.7.stable     GO_BACK #1 at 3351 ms     GO_BACK #2 at 3352 ms     (1 ms)

Its on-screen counter reads 2 after that single press.

This is not one notification reaching several nodes: the MRP has a single Control with a single `_notification`, and nothing else in the project listens.

In my own game the same double quits the app. The first delivery closes the open menu panel and returns; the second finds nothing open and falls through to `get_tree().quit()`. Any handler shaped "close the topmost thing and return, otherwise quit" behaves that way, and a handler that toggles instead ends up a no-op, so Back appears to do nothing.

`targetSdk 36` is the stock default in 4.7, `config.gradle` in `android_source.zip` sets it, and aapt2 reports `targetSdkVersion 36` on the prebuilt `android_debug.apk`. A plain one-click Android export reproduces this.

Suspected origin: #117653, which added an `onBackPressedDispatcher` callback alongside the existing key-event path.

Not a duplicate of #105324, which is one notification reaching handlers in several scenes on 4.4.1. Possibly related: #120638, an ANR on `4.7.stable` at `SDK 36` inside `OnBackPressedDispatcher` the same callback `path.agent` found and reported this to

### Steps to reproduce

1. New project, one scene, this script on the root:
```gdscript
gdscript
extends Control

func _notification(what: int) -> void:
      if what == NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST:
              print("GO_BACK ", Time.get_ticks_msec())
```
2. Set application/config/quit_on_go_back = false.
3. Export to Android with targetSdk 36. Run on a device.

body:
### Tested versions

4.8.dev3, 4.8.dev5

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev5 - Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (1920x1080 @ 60.04 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1235U (12 threads) - 7.48 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I found an issue when using a typed `for` loop with an array literal containing a previously freed object:

`for class_instance: Class in [class_instance_1, class_instance_2]:`

Godot recognizes that the array should be treated as an `Array[Class]`, but typed-array validation appears to reject a `<Freed Object>` value without considering the declared type of the variable. This appears inconsistent with `null`. I would expect the freed-object reference to be accepted by the typed array in the same way as `null`, since the variable itself is statically known to have type `Class`.

This does not appear to cause a functional problem beyond these erroneous error messages:

```
Attempted to set an invalid (previously freed?) object instance into a 'TypedArray'.
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  ./core/variant/container_type_validate.h:97 @ _internal_validate_object()
```

```
Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "set")" is true.
  <C++ Source>  core/variant/array.cpp:518 @ set()
```

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
var ur1 := UndoRedo.new()
var ur2 := UndoRedo.new()

func _init() -> void:
	# This is fine: ur1 = null
	ur1.free()
	for ur: UndoRedo in [ur1, ur2]:
		print(ur)
```

title: Frequent D3D12 freeze/crash from abrupt Full Screen Play-session termination on Windows
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7-stable_win64, 4.6.2-stable_win64, and 4.5.1-stable_win64.

I tested 4.6.2 and 4.5.1-stable_win64 because they had both come out before when I started experiencing this issue which was Feb 2026.

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21045.9003) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (12 threads) - 15.87 GiB memory - WASAPI (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When running a project with `display/window/size/mode` set to full screen and pressing reload current scene or stopping the scene to then run the main scene again, the scene will frequently but not always freeze for a couple seconds before resuming. Sometimes this even results in my graphics device timing out.

I would expect the project to run smoothly, especially when running minimal projects and not cause my graphics device to time out when I am doing no graphically intensive work.

I have observed the freezes to last up to 19 seconds and sometimes crashing with `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET`.

Key details:

- Only reproduces via the editor's Play/Stop/Reload workflow. A standalone (non-editor) launch of the exact same project never reproduces it.

- Only reproduces on D3D12. Vulkan is completely stable on the same hardware/project.

- Not tied to a specific driver version. I've observed this across 8+ AMD driver releases over roughly 7 months.

- Reproduces more reliably the more times Play/Reload is repeated (sometimes within a few cycles, sometimes needs 20-30+)

From my own debugging and an attempted fix, I found the most likely cause to that be stopping or reloading a project kills the running game process with `TerminateProcess()` on Windows. This skips the game's normal shutdown, so the D3D12 swap chain never gets released properly. In fullscreen, that swap chain also gets promoted by Windows to a direct-to-display presentation mode. Killing the process abruptly while it holds this kind of swapchain seems to race with the AMD driver's cleanup of it, and doing this repeatedly (every Stop or Reload) makes the freeze or timeout more likely to happen.

This are the error log that led me to looking into the swapchain in the Godot source code `D3D12: Presenting swapchain failed with error 0x887a0007.` and this is a rejected PR I made for fix that has solved the issue on my device #123393. Hopeful

title: Capturing the mouse while handling mouse event stops propagation
body:
### Tested versions

At least reproducible in 4.5 through 4.8.2

### System information

Windows 10 & Debian 13

### Issue description

#### Issue
If you're setting the [Input::mouse_mode](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#class-input-property-mouse-mode) to [MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#enum-input-mousemode) while handling a mouse event, the mouse event will stop propagating to the next event handlers.

#### Expected behavior

I think the current event propagation should be independent of the mouse_mode, i.e, that the current event finishes its propagation.
The current behavior might be an okay semantic too, as long as there is also a way to choose whether the event finishes its propagation or not.

####  Imperfect (hackish) solution

I initially thought that the following was enough, but it only works some of the time.
```
Input.set_deferred(&"mouse_mode", Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) 
```

#### Extra context

For more context initial *documentation* [issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/issues/11742).
Discussed in this engine [PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123336#issuecomment-5622518020) to document the behavior.
@AThousandShips considers this to be a bug (please correct me if I misunderstood).

### Steps to reproduce

- click on the cube.

### Issue description

AudioServer::Bus::index_cache     (from servers/audio_server.h )  has no class initializer. only assignment to it is inside the mixer.

Every path that makes a Bus assigns name, solo, mute, bypass and volume_db, but never index_cache or soloed

This made my project fail about 15% of the time due to the random value of the uninitialized value (the built-in players resolve their target bus from a notification rather than the mixer)

The scripting API and the internal are also different because it figures out the index by scanning buses, so from gdscript the bus layout is correct yet the actual engine can still be using the stale cache

title: Dictionary invariance not properly checked for `Variant` value type
body:
### Tested versions

- v4.8.dev.custom_build [cb41ea115]

### System information

Fedora 44

### Issue description

Container types with different types are supposed to be invariant. However the GDScript analyzer does not catch a mismatch if the value type is `Variant` (this is probably an oversight from how the untyped exemption is implemented).

This can lead the analyzer to assume types that are not actually verified at runtime. The compiler can generate faulty bytecode based on those types which can lead to crashes in the worst case.

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScrip

func a() -> Dictionary[int, Variant]:
	return {0: 1} as Dictionary[int, Variant]

func b() -> Dictionary[int, String]:
	return a()

func _run() -> void:
	var a := b()[0]
	print(a.bigrams())
```

title: Jolt Physics crashes on 32-bit Windows: MOVAPS into 8-byte-aligned allocations
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable.mono (official Windows `x86_32` export template)
- Not reproducible in: the same project exported `x86_64` (any build)

### System information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (WOW64, `Wow64Guest=0x014C`) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 780 - Vulkan 1.2.142 Forward Mobile

### Issue description

An exported 32-bit Windows game using `physics/3d/physics_engine = "Jolt Physics"` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005)` shortly after the first 3D scene with concave collision loads. The identical project exported for `x86_64` never crashes.

The faulting module is always the engine binary itself, never the game's own library. Across 10 crashes WER recorded three distinct fault offsets, and **every one of them is the same instruction encoding, `0F 29` = `MOVAPS m128, xmm`** — the 16-byte-*aligned* SSE store:

| Fault RVA           | Bytes at that offset                | Instruction                   |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `0x00CDDB80` (7/10) | `0F 29 0A 83 EA 80 0F 29 42 90 ...` | `movaps [edx], xmm1`          |
| `0x00B8FFA6` (2/10) | `0F 29 02 83 C7 0C 83 C3 01 ...`    | `movaps [edx], xmm0`          |
| `0x00BEF2A2` (1/10) | `0F 29 4C 02 10 8B B5 44 FF ...`    | `movaps [edx+eax+0x10], xmm1` |

Two full crash dumps give the register state at the fault:

```
dump 1:  EIP 0x00DFDB80   EDX 0x56FF2588   EDX % 16 = 8   ESI 0x0000C000 (48 KB buffer)
dump 2:  EIP 0x00DFDB80   EDX 0x57A5B248   EDX % 16 = 8   ESI 0x0000C000
```

`EDX` is the destination operand. **It is 8-byte aligned and never 16-byte aligned**, at two different absolute addresses. The 32-bit Windows CRT only guarantees 8-byte alignment from `malloc`; the x64 CRT guarantees 16, which is exactly why the same code path never faults on `x86_64`. Because each allocation is a coin flip, a scene that builds many shapes loses the flip almost immediately.

Note for anyone reproducing: `MOVAPS` on a misaligned operand raises **#GP, not #PF**, so there is no faulting address. Windows synthesises the exception record as `ExceptionInformation = {0, 0xFFFFFFFF}`, and reading `ExceptionInformation[1]` as an address yields a meaningless `0xFFFFFFFF`. The `{0, 0xFFFFFFFF}` pair *is* the misalignment signature; the real operand has to come from the thread `CONTEXT`.

### Where it points

The nearest identifying strings in the code region around `0x00B8FFA6` are from `modules/jolt_physics/shapes/j
